cl_avfx_volclouds_qualitydefault 1 / values 0,1,2Quality preset multiplier applied on top of cl_avfx_volclouds_steps. 0 = low (~0.5x base steps — fastest, mild banding under motion). 1 (default) = quality (~1.0x base steps). 2 = ultra (~1.5x base steps — best fidelity, highest cost). Effective resolved step count is reported in cl_avfx_info under volclouds:.
cl_avfx_volclouds_randomnessdefault 1 / range 0..1 / step 0.05How randomly cloud features are placed across the sky. 0 = highly regular / grid-like pattern; 1 (default) = natural random scatter; 1.0 = maximum disorder. Combined with seed to derive the macro layout.
cl_avfx_volclouds_render_scaledefault 0.5 / range 0.25..1.00 / step 0.05Internal cloud buffer scale. Reserved / informational in this foundation pass (raymarch always runs at scene resolution inside the sky shader). A future optimization phase may add an explicit downscale / temporal-upscale path that uses this cvar; until then it does not change rendering.
cl_avfx_volclouds_seeddefault 40777 / 0 = map/time-derived / non-zero = fixed-offsetCloud noise field seed offset. 40777 (default) = fixed reproducible offset — same cloud layout across reloads and runs. Set to 0 to derive layout from the map / time so it varies between runs. Any non-zero 16-bit value locks a specific arrangement (different seeds = different layouts); combine with evolution_speed 0 to freeze the noise field entirely for screenshots / A-B comparison.
cl_avfx_volclouds_shadow_stepsdefault 0 / range 0..32 / step 1Number of light-march samples toward the sun per raymarch step, for cheap cloud self-shadowing. 0 (default) is a reasonable balance. 0 disables self-shadowing (clouds get only ambient + scatter, no internal darkening). Higher values give richer cloud volume shading but cost grows multiplicatively with main steps.
cl_avfx_volclouds_shape_scaledefault 2.95 / range 0.05..8 / step 0.05Macro shape noise spatial scale. 2.95 (default) gives broad natural cloud cell wavelength. Higher values produce smaller cells (tighter cluster pattern); lower values produce broader continuous overcast.
cl_avfx_volclouds_silver_liningdefault 0.20 / range 0..2 / step 0.05Henyey-Greenstein anisotropy g-factor controlling the silver lining / forward-scatter peak. 0 = isotropic scatter (clouds glow uniformly). Positive values bias scatter forward — bright edges visible when looking toward the sun (the classic silver-lining edge highlight). 0.20 (default) gives a gentle forward-scatter bias.
cl_avfx_volclouds_sizedefault 3.6 / range 0.10..10.0 / step 0.05Macro cloud feature size multiplier. 3.6 (default) gives natural-scale clouds. Higher values produce broader cloud features (looks like puffy cumulus); lower values produce smaller wispier cloud bits. Combines with shape_scale and count to define overall cloud morphology.
cl_avfx_volclouds_size_variationdefault 0.8 / range 0..1 / step 0.05How strongly individual cloud features vary in apparent size. 0 = all clouds the same scale; 0.8 (default) = natural strong variation; 1.0 = strong mix of small and large clouds.
cl_avfx_volclouds_stepsdefault 31 / range 8..128 / step 1Base raymarch sample count per pixel through the cloud slab. 31 (default) is the PO-accepted baseline (the original TZ design value of 48 was lowered after smoke for perf headroom; raise toward 48..96 if the future render-scale audit allows). Effective count = steps × quality_multiplier (see cl_avfx_volclouds_quality). Lower values look stepped / banded; higher values smoother but linearly more expensive.
cl_avfx_volclouds_storm_darkeningdefault 0.25 / range 0..1 / step 0.05Strength of storm-driven cloud darkening. Applied only when both cl_avfx_volclouds 1 AND cl_avfx_storm 1 are active (per Codex Q-C6 binding — no force-enable from weather presets). 0 = clouds unaffected by storm state; 0.25 (default) = clouds visibly darken when storm is on; 1.0 = clouds go nearly black under storm.
cl_avfx_volclouds_sun_lighting0=off / 1=on (default)When ON (default), the sun's direction + power contribute forward-scatter lighting to clouds via the silver-lining curve. When OFF, clouds get only ambient + moon contribution. Independent from sun world-lighting cvars — this controls only the volumetric cloud's response to the sun.
cl_avfx_volclouds_sun_occlusion0=off (default) / 1=onWhen ON, volumetric cloud transmittance attenuates the AVFX sun and moon disk/corona/glow contributions inside the sky shader. Default OFF keeps celestial disks at tuned visibility while accepted flat-cloud occlusion still applies. Per Codex Q-C7 binding — applies to both sun and moon (shared transmittance helper).
cl_avfx_volclouds_temporal_jitterdefault 0 / range 0..1 / step 0.05EXPERIMENTAL v1. Strength of the per-frame temporal sub-step jitter on the volumetric cloud raymarch. The accepted spatial jitter (per-pixel hash of camera + ray) is augmented with a per-frame golden-ratio phase offset; successive frames sample the cloud field at slightly different sub-step starts. v1 (this version) has NO temporal accumulation / feedback (Codex Q-D3.F5.M3 binding for v1), so values >0 produce visible edge shimmer on thin cloud boundaries instead of the smoothed look they would produce with TAA-style accumulation. Default 0.0 (OFF, D2 accepted look). Set to 1.0 to opt into v1 jitter. v2 with feedback / TAA-style accumulation is a queued follow-up that will let this default flip back to ON.
cl_avfx_volclouds_thicknessdefault 2400 / range 64..4096 wu / step 16Thickness (Z-extent) of the cloud slab in world units. 2400 (default) gives a tuned tall vertical extent. Larger values produce thicker clouds with longer raymarch path; smaller values give thin, flat cloud strata. Each raymarch step covers thickness / steps.
cl_avfx_volclouds_trans_cutoff0.001..0.5 (default 0.03)Transmittance level at which the cloud raymarch stops early because the remaining light contribution is negligible. Higher values stop sooner and cost less; lower values march deeper into dense cloud for slightly richer interiors. Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_volclouds 1.
cl_avfx_volclouds_turbulencedefault 0.90 / range 0..1 / step 0.05High-frequency turbulence applied to the cloud density. 0 = smooth clouds; 0.90 (default) = natural strong turbulence; 1.0 = strongly turbulent / chaotic clouds.
cl_avfx_volclouds_wind_dirdefault 351 / range 0..359 deg / step 1Wind direction for cloud drift, in degrees from world +X (math convention — (cos(θ), sin(θ))). 0° points toward world +X (treated as east in standard map orientation). 90° = +Y (north). 180° = -X (west). 270° = -Y (south). 351° (default) is almost +X with a slight south component. Same convention as cl_avfx_sun_azimuth.
cl_avfx_volclouds_wind_speeddefault 20 / range 0..20 / step 0.05Wind speed scalar for cloud drift along cl_avfx_volclouds_wind_dir. Range 0..20. 0 freezes drift (static cloud positions — combine with evolution_speed 0 for fully static field). Low values (1..5) give a gentle slow drift typical of clear-weather skies. 20 (default = maximum) gives the visibly fast storm-sky motion PO accepted as the baseline for the rain preset.
cl_avfx_volclouds_world_shadowdefault 1.25 / range 0..3 / step 0.05Strength of how strongly the SUN-DIRECTION rich cloud transmittance (clouds between the world and the sun, matching the visible Perlin-Worley cloud field) darkens the WORLD BASELINE brightness. Applies the multiplier to the (1 - night_dim) ambient baseline ONLY — sun/moon direction-based contributions are NOT double-dimmed because F1 (cl_avfx_volclouds_lighting_mask) already handles those. 1.25 (default) = tuned dimming when the cloud field covers the sun. 0.0 = clouds do not affect world baseline brightness at all. Higher values up to 3.0 = cinematic dramatic overcast. Applies globally — same surface reads the same brightness regardless of camera position (clouds are a light-filter, not a per-viewer effect). (Legacy zenith/omni sample is kept only as the fallback for the fast value-noise cloud source.)
cl_avfx_volfog0=off (default) / 1=onMaster toggle for AVFX volumetric fog / mist. When ON, the postprocess shader runs a depth-aware screen-space raymarch through a virtual fog layer and composites the result over the scene. Reacts to sun, moon, lightning impacts and the player flashlight. Default OFF — opt-in; new visual layer that adds GPU cost only when enabled. When OFF the shader branch is a single uniform check and costs nothing.
cl_avfx_volfog_anisotropydefault 0.60 / range -0.5..0.9 / step 0.05Henyey-Greenstein anisotropy parameter for sun/moon scatter. Default 0.60 (PO-tuned, stronger forward scatter). 0 = isotropic scatter (fog glows uniformly). Positive values bias scatter forward — fog brightens visibly toward the sun direction (common in real water vapor); negative values bias backward (back-scatter). Moon scatter uses a softer fraction.
cl_avfx_volfog_base_heightdefault 184 / range -4096..4096 wu / step 8Base Z (world units) of the fog layer. Default 184 (PO-tuned low fog baseline). Negative values push the layer below the floor (fog 'leaks' up from below); 0 anchors at the typical floor; positive values lift the layer above the floor.
cl_avfx_volfog_color_bdefault 0.98 / range 0..2 / step 0.01Fog tint blue channel. Default 0.98 (PO-tuned, near-pure cool blue mist). Higher values lean toward azure / cold; lower values produce yellow / brown smoke tints.
cl_avfx_volfog_color_gdefault 0.78 / range 0..2 / step 0.01Fog tint green channel. 0.78 (default). Combined with the red and blue channels to set the base fog color before celestial scatter is applied.
cl_avfx_volfog_color_rdefault 0.7 / range 0..2 / step 0.01Fog tint red channel. 0.7 (default) gives a slightly cool blue-gray fog typical of moist mist. Higher values warm the fog toward red/yellow (smoke / sunset feel); lower values shift to cooler blue. Multiplied with sun/moon scattering to produce the final per-step inscatter color.
cl_avfx_volfog_debugdefault 0 / values 0,1,2,3 (diagnostic, current session only)Debug visualisation mode for the volfog raymarch. 0 = off (normal composite — default). 1 = density: visualise accumulated 1 - transmittance as red (red = denser fog, black = clear). 2 = lighting: visualise raw inscatter color (sun/moon/lightning/flashlight scatter without scene composite). 3 = steps: visualise normalized t_max / view_distance ramp (white = full range, black = clipped near camera). Use for screenshots and tuning; should be 0 in normal play.
cl_avfx_volfog_densitydefault 1.45 / range 0..2 / step 0.05Base fog density (extinction coefficient before height falloff). Default 1.45 (PO-tuned, dense atmospheric fog). Higher values (1.5+) produce thick fog that quickly obscures distant geometry; lower values (0.10) give a thin atmospheric layer. Multiplied with extinction along the raymarch via Beer absorption.
cl_avfx_volfog_evolution_speeddefault 4 / range 0..5 / step 0.05Speed of internal noise evolution (time accumulator multiplier). Default 4 (PO-tuned, noticeable fast morphing of patch shapes). 0.10 gives slow gentle drift suitable for atmospheric haze. Higher values speed up the evolution of patch shapes (independent from wind_speed which only translates the patches). 0 freezes the noise field entirely — useful with non-zero seed for A-B screenshots.
cl_avfx_volfog_extinctiondefault 3.1 / range 0..4 / step 0.05Per-step extinction multiplier (Beer absorption strength). Default 3.10 (PO-tuned, strong per-step absorption — combined with the lower step count of 20 gives a 'patchy thick' look). Lower values make the fog feel more transparent / scattered.
cl_avfx_volfog_falloffdefault 5.45 / range 0.05..8 / step 0.05Density falloff exponent above base_height. Default 5.45 (PO-tuned, tight ground layer below the base plane saturated by ground_hug, very fast decay above it). Lower values (e.g. 1.25) give a slower decay (more fog at the top of the layer). Math: density ∝ exp(-norm_height * falloff) where norm_height = (z - base) / height.
cl_avfx_volfog_flashlight_alphadefault 0.15 / range 0..2 / step 0.05Per-step alpha of the flashlight cone contribution inside the volfog raymarch. Default 0.15 (PO-tuned, soft gentle gradient). Lower values further soften the cone; higher values produce a tight bright spot. 0 disables the flashlight scatter contribution entirely; 2.0 = very bright cone. Scoped to the fog raymarch only — does NOT change the accepted flashlight surface boost on BSP / entity materials.
cl_avfx_volfog_flashlight_scatter0=off / 1=on (default)When ON (default), the player flashlight cone scatters fog inside the cone — produces a visible volumetric beam. Uses the raw cone boost (no surface_alpha cap, per Codex Q-L2 binding — matches accepted rain-particle behavior), so the volumetric beam is visible even when the cone has not reached a surface. Respects flashlight master / intensity / battery / range / angle. When OFF, flashlight has no effect on fog scattering.
cl_avfx_volfog_ground_hug0=off / 1=on (default)When ON (default), points below base_height are saturated with fog density (the fog 'pools' on the floor and lower areas). When OFF, density below the base layer is 0 (fog exists only above the base plane). Use OFF if you want fog as a high bank with clear space at the floor.
cl_avfx_volfog_heightdefault 3504 / range 0..4096 wu / step 16Thickness of the fog layer (world units) above base_height. Default 3504 (PO-tuned, thick layer covering most of the vertical extent of typical maps). Smaller values (e.g. 256) keep fog low along the floor. Combined with falloff for the exact density curve.
cl_avfx_volfog_lightning_scatter0=off / 1=on (default)When ON (default), real AVFX lightning strike impacts brighten nearby fog with a per-strike exponential falloff (~512 wu half-distance per Codex Q-L1 binding). Fades with the bolt brightness envelope. Combined contribution is clamped to prevent whiteout under cluster strikes. Visual-only — does NOT change lightning damage.
cl_avfx_volfog_moon_scatter0=off / 1=on (default)When ON (default), the moon's cool color and phase contribute a weak cold scatter to fog at night. When OFF, moonless behaviour applies regardless of moon state. Per Codex Q-L3 binding — much weaker than sun by design.
cl_avfx_volfog_near_fadedefault 344 / range 0..2048 wu / step 8Distance window over which the fog opacity smoothly fades in starting at start_distance. Default 344 (PO-tuned). Higher values widen the fade (fog only fully contributes far from the camera), lower values harden the boundary. Visual-only — does not change the raymarch range.
cl_avfx_volfog_noisedefault 0.75 / range 0..1 / step 0.05Strength of the low-frequency noise patches that break the fog into uneven puffs. Default 0.75 (PO-tuned, visible patchiness). 1.0 = maximum patchiness; 0 = perfectly smooth uniform layer. Combined with noise_scale and patchiness for the full effect.
cl_avfx_volfog_noise_scaledefault 5.45 / range 0.05..8 / step 0.05Spatial scale of the noise patches. 5.45 (default) gives small active wisps. Higher values shrink patches further; lower values make broad uniform-ish patches. Combined with wind_dir/wind_speed patches drift with wind.
cl_avfx_volfog_opacitydefault 0.70 / range 0..1 / step 0.05Final opacity scalar of the fog composite over the scene. Default 0.70 (PO-tuned, scene clearly visible through dense fog). 1.0 = fog fully obscures at max accumulated density; 0 disables visual contribution while keeping the raymarch active (use the debug modes to inspect).
cl_avfx_volfog_patchinessdefault 0.5 / range 0..1 / step 0.05Amplitude of the noise patches — how strongly density varies between dense and thin patches. 0.5 (default) gives natural variation. Higher values (close to 1.0) produce extreme dense/thin contrast — fog looks 'broken' into clusters; lower values keep the fog more uniform with just light texture.
cl_avfx_volfog_qualitydefault 0 / values 0,1,2Quality preset for volumetric fog raymarch. 0 = low (default, beta performance profile), 1 = quality, 2 = ultra (≈25% more steps for smoother dense fog). Effective step count is reported in cl_avfx_info.
cl_avfx_volfog_render_scaledefault 0.40 / range 0.25..1.00 / step 0.05Performance scale for volumetric fog raymarch steps. 0.40 (default) cuts the effective full-resolution sample count; 1.00 uses the full requested step count. A real low-res fog buffer is a later optimization.
cl_avfx_volfog_seeddefault 24030 / any 16-bit integer for a fixed-offset layoutNoise seed for the patch layout offset. Default 24030 = accepted fixed layout. 0 = no offset (the noise field drifts naturally via wind + evolution_speed). Non-zero shifts the entire noise field by a fixed amount along the time axis — different seeds produce different starting layouts of the same field. Combined with evolution_speed > 0 the layout still drifts; set evolution_speed=0 to freeze a specific layout for screenshots / A-B comparison.
cl_avfx_volfog_start_distancedefault 248 / range 0..2048 wu / step 8Distance from camera (world units) where the fog raymarch starts contributing. Default 248 (PO-tuned clear near-field zone). Set higher for a wider clear near-field zone (useful when the camera is in a small room and you want fog only farther away).
cl_avfx_volfog_stepsdefault 10 / range 8..128 / step 1Requested raymarch samples per pixel. Default 10 in the beta performance profile. The effective count is adjusted by cl_avfx_volfog_quality and cl_avfx_volfog_render_scale; low/0.40 defaults to 4 effective samples.
cl_avfx_volfog_sun_scatter0=off / 1=on (default)When ON (default), the sun's color + altitude-driven power contributes to fog inscatter via Henyey-Greenstein phase function. Bright at noon, warm at sunrise/sunset, dim at night (when sun is below horizon). When OFF, fog stays at the user tint baseline regardless of sun position — useful to keep fog 'theatrical' / off-physics.
cl_avfx_volfog_view_distancedefault 4096 / range 128..8192 wu / step 16Maximum raymarch distance in world units. Default 4096 in the beta performance profile; 8192 remains available for full-map haze. Lower values cap how far fog extends visibly. The fog accumulates between start_distance and min(view_distance, surface_depth).
cl_avfx_volfog_wind_dirdefault 267 / range 0..359 deg / step 1Wind direction for fog patch drift, in degrees. Default 267 (PO-tuned, ≈ WSW). 0 = +X (east), 90 = +Y (north), 180 = -X (west), 270 = -Y (south). Convention matches cl_avfx_sun_azimuth. Combined with wind_speed to drift the noise patches across the scene over time.
cl_avfx_volfog_wind_speeddefault 10 / range 0..10 / step 0.05Wind speed scalar applied to noise patch drift. Default 10 (PO-tuned, visibly fast storm-style scrolling). Lower values (e.g. 0.35) give slow gentle motion suitable for ground mist. 0 stops all patch motion (static fog).
cl_avfx_water0=stock warp (default) / 1=enhanced water (requires cl_avfx_world 1)Enhanced water surface master toggle. 0 (default) — stock Q2 warp surface unchanged. 1 — when cl_avfx_world is also on, water surfaces get an extended shader path with subtle animated normal/ripple distortion, optional natural water color correction (cl_avfx_water_color), specular/highlight motion, weather-strength-driven amplitude, and an optional rain-impact ring overlay layer. Lava and slime surfaces are explicitly excluded.
cl_avfx_water_celestial_lighting0=off / 1=on (default)Master toggle for water + puddle celestial lighting response. When ON (default), real BSP water surfaces, AVFX puddle overlays, runoff streams, foam bubbles, puddle rings and falling-water droplets react to the accepted celestial state. At noon water stays close to the accepted bright daytime look; at sunrise/sunset it picks up a subtle warm/cool mood; at moonlit night it becomes darker and colder; at moonless night it darkens strongly to a deep cold tint near the minimum brightness floor. When OFF, water returns to the daytime-bright behavior regardless of sun/moon state. Independent from cl_avfx_sun_lighting / cl_avfx_moon_lighting. Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_water 1.
cl_avfx_water_celestial_min_brightnessdefault 0.05 / range 0..1 / step 0.01Minimum water brightness floor when there is no celestial light. Set lower than the snow floor (water can naturally read very dark at night). 0.05 (default) keeps moonless deep-night water as a very dim cold tint, not pure black. 0 = no floor (water goes fully dark when celestial light disappears). Higher values keep water visibly bright at night (less convincing).
cl_avfx_water_celestial_night_tintdefault 0.55 / range 0..1 / step 0.05How much cold deep-blue tint water picks up in low-light conditions. Stronger than the snow tint (0.45) because night water reads as deep cold blue/teal rather than grey-white. 0.55 (default) gives a natural night mood for moonlit / moonless water. The night tint is applied via mix(water_rgb, water_rgb × cold_color (0.35, 0.48, 0.68), (1 − max_light) × this). 0 = no cold tint. 1 = strongest cold push.
cl_avfx_water_celestial_specular_scaledefault 1.00 / range 0..2 / step 0.05Multiplier for the brightness scalar exposed to CPU-only water highlight paths (foam bubbles, runoff streams, puddle rings, falling-water droplets) that do not receive the shader's final RGB multiply. The water shader paths (GLS_AVFX_WATER + GLS_AVFX_PUDDLE) handle their own specular/foam scaling automatically via the final end-of-block RGB multiply — this cvar is reserved for future per-effect tuning on the CPU paths and currently affects only the brightness-scalar diagnostic output.
cl_avfx_water_celestial_strengthdefault 1.00 / range 0..2 / step 0.05How strongly celestial sun + moon illumination drives water color/brightness. 1.00 (default) gives a natural balance between identity-at-noon and visible night darkening. 0 = water color is driven entirely by the minimum brightness floor and night tint (no sun/moon influence). Up to 2.0 = strong reaction to sun/moon state. This is the artistic knob on top of the physically-emergent formula base + strength × (sun_part + moon_part).
cl_avfx_water_clarity0..1 (menu step 0.05, default 0.35)Water clarity; higher = see deeper before it darkens (0..1, default 0.35). Requires realistic water plus at least one depth feature — cl_avfx_water_depth_color 1 or cl_avfx_water_shore_foam 1; otherwise the whole depth lane is published as zero.
cl_avfx_water_color0=original / 1=natural (default) / 2=clear / 3=tropical / 4=pool / 5=ocean / 6=lake / 7=glacier / 8=deep / 9=murky / 10=toxicWater color correction profile. Wide palette of natural and artificial water looks; mix() blend in the fragment shader applies live (no vid_restart needed). 0=original (no tint). 1=natural (default — soft cool blue, balanced). 2=clear (bright cyan, crystal pool). 3=tropical (vivid turquoise, lagoon). 4=pool (chlorinated bright blue). 5=ocean (saturated deep blue). 6=lake (greenish-blue, low saturation). 7=glacier (pale ice blue, high brightness). 8=deep (very dark abyssal). 9=murky (dark olive-green swamp). 10=toxic (sickly yellow-green hazard). Profiles only apply on water surfaces (lava / slime untouched). Effective only when cl_avfx_water is on.
cl_avfx_water_deep_mix0..1 (menu step 0.05, default 1)Amount of dark deep tint mixed into deep water (0..1, default 1.0). Requires realistic water plus at least one depth feature — cl_avfx_water_depth_color 1 or cl_avfx_water_shore_foam 1; otherwise the whole depth lane is published as zero.
cl_avfx_water_depth_color0=Off / 1=On (default 1)Depth-based colouring: shallow shore lighter, deep water darker/bluer. On by default; needs Realistic water (uses a scene-depth snapshot). Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1 + cl_avfx_water 1 + cl_avfx_water_realistic 1, and enables the pre-water opaque depth snapshot, so it costs more than plain enhanced water.
cl_avfx_water_depth_color_strength0..2 (menu step 0.05, default 0.85)Strength of the depth colouring (0..2, default 0.85). Requires realistic water plus at least one depth feature — cl_avfx_water_depth_color 1 or cl_avfx_water_shore_foam 1; otherwise the whole depth lane is published as zero.
cl_avfx_water_depth_extinction0.1..4 (menu step 0.05, default 1.15)How fast water darkens with depth (0.1..4, default 1.15). Requires realistic water plus at least one depth feature — cl_avfx_water_depth_color 1 or cl_avfx_water_shore_foam 1; otherwise the whole depth lane is published as zero.
cl_avfx_water_foam0=no drifting foam (default) / 1=drifting patchesDrifting foam patches across the water surface — small white patches that smoothly fade in, drift slowly with time, then fade out, simulating real-water foam. Two-octave noise (large rare patches + smaller faster ones) with cell-grid distortion so the pattern reads organic, not geometric. 0 (default) — no patches. 1 — patches appear and drift. Intensity is scaled by cl_avfx_water_strength; when cl_avfx_world_auto is on heavy rain / storm boost the amount.
cl_avfx_water_fresnel_power1..8 (menu step 0.1, default 2.8)Fresnel falloff exponent. Higher = reflection only at the very grazing edge (1..8, default 2.80). Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1 + cl_avfx_water 1 + cl_avfx_water_realistic 1; it has no effect on baseline enhanced water.
cl_avfx_water_fresnel_strength0..2 (menu step 0.05, default 1.2)Strength of grazing-angle sky reflection (fresnel) on realistic water (0..2, default 1.20). Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1 + cl_avfx_water 1 + cl_avfx_water_realistic 1; it has no effect on baseline enhanced water.
cl_avfx_water_model_reflection0/1 (default 0)Master toggle for MODEL reflections on BSP water. The per-category toggles below (weapons / armor / items / players+monsters / ships / meteors / comets / planets) choose what reflects; all default OFF.
cl_avfx_water_model_reflection_actors0/1 (default 0)Reflect player and monster models on BSP water. Needs the water MODEL-reflection master on. Default OFF.
cl_avfx_water_model_reflection_armor0/1 (default 0)Reflect armor models on BSP water. Needs the water MODEL-reflection master on. Default OFF.
cl_avfx_water_model_reflection_comets0/1 (default 0)Reflect AVFX comets on BSP water. Needs the water MODEL-reflection master on. Default OFF.
cl_avfx_water_model_reflection_items0/1 (default 0)Reflect item / object models on BSP water. Needs the water MODEL-reflection master on. Default OFF.
cl_avfx_water_model_reflection_meteors0/1 (default 0)Reflect AVFX sky meteors (shooting-star streaks + embers) on BSP water. Needs the water MODEL-reflection master on. Default OFF.
cl_avfx_water_model_reflection_planets0/1 (default 0)Reflect the AVFX Earth, Moon, Sun, Black Hole and compatible celestial bodies on BSP water (per-pixel reflected-ray disk + a spatial BSP line-of-sight mask, same path as puddles). Needs AVFX world, visible water and the water model-reflection master. Each body also needs its own master enabled, so this category plus cl_avfx_blackhole is the complete gate for the Black Hole — there is deliberately no separate black-hole reflection toggle. Default OFF.
cl_avfx_water_model_reflection_projectiles0/1 (default 0)Reflect final presented projectiles and the rail beam on BSP water, including synchronized local prediction. Needs the water model-reflection master. Default OFF.
cl_avfx_water_model_reflection_quality0 Performance; 1 Medium; 2 Quality; 3 Ultra; 4 Extra (default)Quality budget for object reflections on BSP water. Lower tiers smoothly fade distant models, reduce reflected sky-object populations and keep only the nearest water receiver faces. Extra preserves the complete current image.
cl_avfx_water_model_reflection_ships0/1 (default 0)Reflect AVFX sky spaceships on BSP water. Needs the water MODEL-reflection master on. Default OFF.
cl_avfx_water_model_reflection_strength0..1 (default 0.8)Strength / opacity of model reflections on BSP water.
cl_avfx_water_model_reflection_surface_volumes0/1 (default 0)Reflect placed Surface Volumes (steam, smoke and fog) on transparent and opaque BSP water. Needs the water model-reflection master. Default OFF.
cl_avfx_water_model_reflection_weapons0/1 (default 0)Reflect weapon models on BSP water. Needs the water MODEL-reflection master on. Default OFF.
cl_avfx_water_normal_strength0..2 (menu step 0.05, default 1.65)Strength of the procedural surface normal; drives fresnel/glint brightness (0..2, default 1.65). Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1 + cl_avfx_water 1 + cl_avfx_water_realistic 1; it has no effect on baseline enhanced water.
cl_avfx_water_quality0=low / 1=normal (default) / 2=highEnhanced water shader detail tier. 0=low (cheaper distortion, fewer wave layers), 1=normal (default, balanced), 2=high (more distortion samples + extra specular passes). Quality tier caps the per-water-surface shader cost; PO can drop to 0 on weak GPUs without losing the water identity, or push to 2 for screenshots / cinematic feel. Effective only when cl_avfx_water is on.
cl_avfx_water_realistic0=Off / 1=On (default 0)Optional realistic mode layered over enhanced water: procedural waves and normals, grazing-angle fresnel sky reflection and sun glint. Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1 + cl_avfx_water 1; it is an opt-in, so the accepted baseline water stays byte-identical while it is off. Costs an extra wave/normal plus fresnel evaluation on every water fragment.
cl_avfx_water_reflection_distort0..1 (default 0)Liquid distortion of ALL water reflections (SSR + models + sky objects), scaled by the water surface speed. 0 = sharp mirror.
cl_avfx_water_reflection_distort_speed0..5 (default 1)Speed of the water reflection ripple. 1 = default, 0 = frozen ripple.
cl_avfx_water_ripples0=smooth surface / 1=animated wavelets (default)Enhanced water surface RIPPLE OVERLAY layer (separate from cl_avfx_rain_water_ripples — that one is the per-drop ring buffer, this is the surface-shader ripple amplitude). 0 — water surface stays smooth. 1 (default) — adds animated wavelets across the water plane, amplitude scaled by cl_avfx_water_strength + (when cl_avfx_world_auto is on) the current weather strength. Effective only when cl_avfx_water is on.
cl_avfx_water_scene_reflection0/1 (default 0)Screen-space reflection (SSR) of nearby world geometry on BSP water. Reflects only on-screen geometry; MODEL and sky-object reflections are separate toggles below.
cl_avfx_water_scene_reflection_strength0..1Strength / opacity of the water SSR reflection.
cl_avfx_water_shore_foam0=Off / 1=On (default 1)Shore foam where clear shallow water meets the shore/geometry. On by default; needs Realistic water + depth snapshot. 1.4: not drawn on opaque water (q2dm1). Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1 + cl_avfx_water 1 + cl_avfx_water_realistic 1, and enables the pre-water opaque depth snapshot, so it costs more than plain enhanced water.
cl_avfx_water_shore_foam_alpha0..1 (menu step 0.05, default 0.35)Opacity of shore foam (0..1, default 0.35), separate from brightness. Lower = dissolves more into the water. Requires cl_avfx_water_realistic 1 + cl_avfx_water_shore_foam 1; the foam pass also consumes the pre-water opaque depth snapshot.
cl_avfx_water_shore_foam_intensity0..2 (menu step 0.05, default 1.35)Brightness of the shore foam (0..2, default 1.35). Requires cl_avfx_water_realistic 1 + cl_avfx_water_shore_foam 1; the foam pass also consumes the pre-water opaque depth snapshot.
cl_avfx_water_shore_foam_noise0..1 (menu step 0.05, default 0)Noise break-up of the foam; higher = less solid (0..1, default 0). Requires cl_avfx_water_realistic 1 + cl_avfx_water_shore_foam 1; the foam pass also consumes the pre-water opaque depth snapshot.
cl_avfx_water_shore_foam_range0..1 (menu step 0.05, default 0.15)How far foam reaches out from shore (0..1, default 0.15). Higher = wider foam band. Requires cl_avfx_water_realistic 1 + cl_avfx_water_shore_foam 1; the foam pass also consumes the pre-water opaque depth snapshot.
cl_avfx_water_shore_foam_size0.25..4 (menu step 0.05, default 1)Size of foam texture elements (0.25..4, default 1.0). Lower = finer foam, higher = larger blobs. Requires cl_avfx_water_realistic 1 + cl_avfx_water_shore_foam 1; the foam pass also consumes the pre-water opaque depth snapshot.
cl_avfx_water_shore_foam_speed0..3 (menu step 0.05, default 3)Foam animation speed (0..3, default 3.0). Requires cl_avfx_water_realistic 1 + cl_avfx_water_shore_foam 1; the foam pass also consumes the pre-water opaque depth snapshot.
cl_avfx_water_shore_mix0..1 (menu step 0.05, default 0.5)Amount of light shore tint mixed into shallow water (0..1, default 0.50). Requires realistic water plus at least one depth feature — cl_avfx_water_depth_color 1 or cl_avfx_water_shore_foam 1; otherwise the whole depth lane is published as zero.
cl_avfx_water_sky_reflection0..1 (default 0.75)How much sky / cloud colour is reflected on BSP water surfaces. A cheap procedural sky tint, independent of SSR / model reflections (those are separate toggles).
cl_avfx_water_specular_strength0..2 (menu step 0.05, default 0.65)Sun-glint strength along the realistic-water wave normal (0..2, default 0.65). Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1 + cl_avfx_water 1 + cl_avfx_water_realistic 1; it has no effect on baseline enhanced water.
cl_avfx_water_strength0..1 (default 0.5)Enhanced water visual strength multiplier, 0..1. 0 = no extra effect (matches cl_avfx_water 0 even when the master is on). 0.5 (default) = balanced subtle ripples + colour correction. 1.0 = maximum visible distortion + colour shift. Combines multiplicatively with weather-strength biasing when cl_avfx_world_auto is on.
cl_avfx_water_surface_speed0.1..10 (default 1.0)BSP water style motion speed multiplier. 1.0 (default) = the accepted baseline; 0.1 = 10x slower, 10 = 10x faster. Scales all selected-style motion (downhill flow + ripple warp + cross-blend). No effect at style 0 (Standard).
cl_avfx_water_surface_style0..12 (default 0)BSP water surface material style. 0 = Standard (exact current look, no style texture). 1..12 = reference-derived water tiles (clear shallow, pool caustics, ripples, ocean chop, deep, lagoon, foam, etc.) at pics/q2prox/avfx/ws/. Material DETAIL only — adds caustic/ripple/specular breakup and restrained color; cl_avfx_water_color still drives hue. Does NOT gate any AVFX water effect (rings, foam, realistic water, celestial, lightning). Works in baseline and realistic water. Live, no vid_restart; missing tile falls back to Standard.
cl_avfx_water_wave_scale0.25..4 (menu step 0.05, default 1.7)Tiling scale of the realistic-water wave normal (0.25..4, default 1.70). Lower = larger waves. Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1 + cl_avfx_water 1 + cl_avfx_water_realistic 1; it has no effect on baseline enhanced water.
cl_avfx_water_wave_speed0..3 (menu step 0.05, default 1)Wave animation speed of realistic water (0..3, default 1.0). Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1 + cl_avfx_water 1 + cl_avfx_water_realistic 1; it has no effect on baseline enhanced water.
cl_avfx_water_wind_coupling0..1 (menu step 0.05, default 1)Couples wave direction to wind / anisotropy (0..1, default 1.0). Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1 + cl_avfx_water 1 + cl_avfx_water_realistic 1; it has no effect on baseline enhanced water.
cl_avfx_weapon_impact_bfg0=off / 1=on (default)Enable AVFX water-impact reaction for the BFG. Visual: huge steam cloud + large irregular dark/evaporation stain that fades back cleanly over ~17 seconds. Client-side visual only — does not mutate gameplay, BSP contents, or server state. Currently the puddle alpha inside the BFG halo is NOT live-suppressed (a follow-up adds the alpha hook); existing visible puddles fade naturally while the stain occludes them.
cl_avfx_weapon_impact_blaster0=off / 1=on (default)Enable AVFX water-impact reaction for the Blaster. Only effective when cl_avfx_weapon_impacts is 1. Visual: small splash + small spray + a few water rings + a single steam puff with the AVFX steam hiss audio (steam_hiss1..3.wav, gated by cl_avfx_audio_lava_steam).
cl_avfx_weapon_impact_chaingun0=off / 1=on (default)Enable AVFX water-impact reaction for the Chaingun. Same family as Machinegun but richer because more bullets hit; rate-capped to avoid particle/audio flood.
cl_avfx_weapon_impact_debugdefault 0 / 0=off, >0=diagnostic (diagnostic, current session only)Developer-only: AVFX weapon-impact diagnostic overlay/print. 0=off. Not archived, no menu; zero cost at 0.
cl_avfx_weapon_impact_grenadelauncher0=off / 1=on (default)Enable AVFX water-impact reaction for the Grenade Launcher. Same family as Hand Grenade with slight per-grenade variation; irregular fading dark stains. Note: Q2 protocol uses the same TE for hand-thrown grenades and Grenade Launcher rounds, so opponent hand grenades also go through this cvar.
cl_avfx_weapon_impact_handgrenade0=off / 1=on (default)Enable AVFX water-impact reaction for the Hand Grenade. Visual: large splash/fountain (~5x the Railgun) + more and larger rings + an irregular semi-transparent dark stain on water that fades over time. Stain shape varies per hit via seeded fan extents.
cl_avfx_weapon_impact_hyperblaster0=off / 1=on (default)Enable AVFX water-impact reaction for the Hyperblaster. Each projectile hit on water spawns the Blaster-style effect, but the per-frame visual gate caps the rate to avoid particle/audio flood under continuous fire.
cl_avfx_weapon_impact_machinegun0=off / 1=on (default)Enable AVFX water-impact reaction for the Machinegun. Visual: bullet splash + small water rings, no steam. Burst fire reads as a dotted bullet line on water as each bullet TE arrives.
cl_avfx_weapon_impact_railgun0=off / 1=on (default)Enable AVFX water-impact reaction for the Railgun. Visual: fountain/splash at the water impact point + many water rings + steam effect with AVFX steam hiss.
cl_avfx_weapon_impact_rocketlauncher0=off / 1=on (default)Enable AVFX water-impact reaction for the Rocket Launcher. Visual: huge fountain/splash at rocket impact + many sprays in all directions + many rings + large irregular semi-transparent dark stain fading over time + strong steam using AVFX steam hiss.
cl_avfx_weapon_impact_shotgun0=off / 1=on (default)Enable AVFX water-impact reaction for the Shotgun. Visual: pellet-based scattered splash pattern + rings/spray per pellet group; no steam. Note: Q2 protocol does not distinguish Shotgun from Super Shotgun pellets, so opponent SSG fire also goes through this cvar; pellet count carries the visual difference.
cl_avfx_weapon_impact_supershotgun0=off / 1=on (default)Enable AVFX water-impact reaction for the Super Shotgun. Same as Shotgun but stronger/richer and wider, accounting for the larger pellet spread. No steam.
cl_avfx_weapon_impacts0=off (default) / 1=enable weapon water impactsMaster toggle for AVFX reactions when weapons hit real water (CONTENTS_WATER) or visibly rendered AVFX puddles / flow surfaces. Lava/slime are NOT routed here — the existing lava-steam path already handles those. Effects per weapon: blaster/hyperblaster — splash + few rings + steam hiss; machinegun/chaingun — bullet splash + small rings, no steam; shotgun/SSG — pellet pattern splash + rings, no steam; railgun — fountain + many rings + steam; hand grenade / grenade launcher — large splash + irregular fading dark stain; rocket launcher — huge fountain + radial spray + irregular fading dark stain + strong steam; BFG — huge steam cloud + large irregular evaporation stain that fades back over ~17 seconds (client-side visual only). Per-weapon toggles below allow disabling individual families.
cl_avfx_weapon_snow_impact_bfg0=off / 1=on (default)Enable AVFX snow-impact reaction for the BFG. Visual: giant melted/burned area covering several meters around the hit + 8 radial steam puffs. Mark fades back as snow refills. Client-side visual only.
cl_avfx_weapon_snow_impact_blaster0=off / 1=on (default)Enable AVFX snow-impact reaction for the Blaster. Visual: small dark-warm melted patch on snow + light snow dust upward + one steam puff using AVFX steam hiss.
cl_avfx_weapon_snow_impact_chaingun0=off / 1=on (default)Enable AVFX snow-impact reaction for the Chaingun. Same family as Machinegun, denser dust and holes per shot.
cl_avfx_weapon_snow_impact_fade_rate0.1..20.0 (default 1.0)Multiplier over the snow refill speed that controls how fast weapon marks (bullet pinholes, melted spots, craters) disappear. Mirrors the footprint fade-rate semantics but applies to the weapon snow mark pool only. 1.0 = normal (same speed as snow accumulation); 0.1 = roughly 10x longer-lived marks; 10..20 = much faster fill-in. No effect on water/lava effects.
cl_avfx_weapon_snow_impact_grenadelauncher0=off / 1=on (default)Enable AVFX snow-impact reaction for the Grenade Launcher. Same family as Hand Grenade with slight per-grenade seeded variation.
cl_avfx_weapon_snow_impact_handgrenade0=off / 1=on (default)Enable AVFX snow-impact reaction for the Hand Grenade. Visual: very large snow crater/mark + big snow fountain + steam. Stain shape varies per hit via seeded fan extents.
cl_avfx_weapon_snow_impact_hyperblaster0=off / 1=on (default)Enable AVFX snow-impact reaction for the Hyperblaster. Same family as Blaster per projectile; rate-capped to avoid dust/audio flood.
cl_avfx_weapon_snow_impact_machinegun0=off / 1=on (default)Enable AVFX snow-impact reaction for the Machinegun. Visual: small dark cool-grey bullet pinhole in snow + small snow dust burst upward; no steam.
cl_avfx_weapon_snow_impact_railgun0=off / 1=on (default)Enable AVFX snow-impact reaction for the Railgun. Visual: large dark melted patch on snow + strong snow dust upward + 2 steam puffs using AVFX steam hiss.
cl_avfx_weapon_snow_impact_rocketlauncher0=off / 1=on (default)Enable AVFX snow-impact reaction for the Rocket Launcher. Visual: huge snow crater + huge snow fountain + 6 radial dust sprays + 4 steam puffs. Strongest non-BFG explosive snow reaction.
cl_avfx_weapon_snow_impact_shotgun0=off / 1=on (default)Enable AVFX snow-impact reaction for the Shotgun. Visual: scattered pellet pinholes + strong snow dust burst. Pellet count carries the per-shot density naturally.
cl_avfx_weapon_snow_impact_supershotgun0=off / 1=on (default)Enable AVFX snow-impact reaction for the Super Shotgun. Same as Shotgun but stronger/richer and wider scatter — roughly 2x SHG visual on snow.
cl_avfx_weapon_snow_impacts0=off (default) / 1=enable weapon snow impactsMaster toggle for AVFX reactions when weapons hit visible snow (surface field + GPU material coverage above the visible threshold). Effects: thermal weapons (blaster/HB/rail/rocket/BFG) melt/burn snow + raise steam; bullets (MG/CG/SHG/SSG) punch dark holes + throw snow dust; explosives (HG/GL/RL) carve craters + throw snow fountains; BFG melts a large patch. Effects scale with visible snow body and snowdrift POM growth. Marks fade as snow refills them. Snow detection runs after water/lava detection fails so liquid hits keep priority. Requires cl_avfx_weapon_impacts 1 as well.
cl_avfx_weapon_snow_steam_audio0=off / 1=on (default)Separate audio gate for steam caused by hot weapon impacts on snow (blaster / hyperblaster / rail / explosives / BFG). Visual steam remains controlled by the per-weapon snow-impact toggles; this cvar only enables or disables the hiss sound, independent of lava steam audio.
cl_avfx_weather_level0=light/quiet / 1=normal (default) / 2=heavyWeather strength selector — biases visual density, fall speed, raindrop density, wind ambience, rain ambience and storm event chance toward light/normal/heavy without overwriting your manual sliders. You can still combine "heavy visuals + quiet audio" or "light streaks + loud wind" via the detailed cvars.
cl_avfx_weather_renderer0=Classic / 1=Accelerated / 2=Auto (default 2)Weather render path. Classic uses the legacy CPU/entity path. Accelerated/Auto can use the modern path when the AVFX backend is Accelerated. Requires cl_avfx 1. The accelerated path is used only when cl_avfx_backend 1 is also set; Auto falls back to the classic path whenever the accelerated one is unavailable.
cl_avfx_wind_x-512..512 (default 0)Wind X component (world units / second). Slants rain streaks and drifts particles eastward (+) or westward (-).
cl_avfx_wind_y-512..512 (default 0)Wind Y component (world units / second). Slants rain streaks and drifts particles north (+) or south (-).
cl_avfx_world0=off (default) / 1=onAVFX master toggle for world / surface effects. 0 (default) — none of the optional surface content is rendered (water surface enhancements, weather-driven sky, rain splashes / puddles, water ripples, snow accumulation). 1 — decorative content is enabled, individually gated by per-feature cvars (cl_avfx_water, cl_avfx_sky, cl_avfx_rain_impacts, cl_avfx_snow_accum, etc.). The mandatory liquid-volume clipping that prevents AVFX particles from rendering inside water / lava / slime is always active when AVFX itself is on, independent of this toggle.
cl_avfx_world_auto0=manual per-feature / 1=auto-coupled to weather (default)Auto-coupling between weather state and surface effects. 1 (default) — heavier rain / snow / storm automatically increases sky darkness, cloud intensity, ripple density, splash count and puddle coverage proportionally. 0 — surface effects use only their own per-feature strength cvars without weather coupling. Auto-coupling makes weather presets feel physically connected to the world; manual mode is useful when the user wants explicit control of each effect intensity independent of AVFX preset / weather level.
cl_avfx_world_debug0=basic info (default) / 1=detail (diagnostic, current session only)Surface-effects diagnostic text in the cl_avfx_info dump. 0 (default) — standard AVFX info only. 1 — adds surface detail: liquid-volume clipping stats (camera-in-liquid status, per-particle clip counts), surface classifier counts, ripple / splash / puddle / snow accumulation event counts, last-clear reason. Not archived; resets to 0 on restart.
cl_avfxgen_airdefault 0 / 0=Random / 1=Off / 2=Ash / 3=Dust / 4=MistAVFX Preset Generator: secondary airborne impurity selector. Random resolves to Off when the main profile is Off and never duplicates the main Ash/Dust/Mist identity, matching the engine's air-layer rules; an explicitly impossible fixed pair (Off main with an impurity, or an identical pair) refuses generation with an explanation and changes nothing. Saved to the global Q2PRO-X config; never part of any AVFX preset snapshot.
cl_avfxgen_atmospheredefault 0 / 0=Random / 1=Off / 2=Lightning / 3=Volumetric fog / 4=Clouds / 5=Fog and clouds / 6=All compatibleAVFX Preset Generator: atmospheric-effects selector. Lightning requires the Rain atmosphere: with a Random main profile a fixed Lightning resolves it to Rain+Storm, with a fixed incompatible profile the request is refused atomically. Clouds cover the flat sky overlay plus quality-eligible volumetric clouds; Fog and clouds combines both; All compatible enables everything the tier, budget and weather allow. Inert until Generate; never part of any AVFX preset snapshot.
cl_avfxgen_celestialdefault 0 / 0=Random / 1=Off / 3=Sun / 5=Planets/Earth / 9=Black Hole / 10=All compatibleAVFX Preset Generator: celestial-bodies selector, limited to Sun, planets/Earth and Black Hole. Random may produce none, one, several or all tier-allowed bodies; every fixed choice is exact. Black Hole implies the required star backdrop and needs Ultra Quality; planets/Earth need Balanced. Meteors, comets and spaceships are controlled independently by cl_avfxgen_traffic. Inert until Generate; never part of any AVFX preset snapshot.
cl_avfxgen_chaosdefault 0 / 0=Full / 1=ReasonableAVFX Preset Generator: chaos level. Full (default) varies the appearance of every active family — shape, color, movement, surfaces, sky, celestial bodies — using quantized values from accepted presets and curated safe points of the guided menu ranges, inside the quality tier's budget; each active family always makes at least one visible style decision (signature axes and coherent palettes). Reasonable reproduces the original curated generator exactly. Inert until Generate is pressed; never part of any AVFX preset snapshot.
cl_avfxgen_coveragedefault 1 / 0=Random / 1=FullAVFX Preset Generator: surface coverage zone. Full drives every active surface material that has a coverage amount to its maximum — mold, greenery, brick, cracks and the floor and wall coverings; the two covering layers additionally use Uniform distribution. Random leaves those amounts to the generator. This selector decides placement area, not participation or opacity. Wildlife and wall runoff are never touched, and Surface Drawings never take part in generation. Inert until Generate; never part of an AVFX preset snapshot.
cl_avfxgen_materialsdefault 1 / 0=Random / 1=Always / 2=OffAVFX Preset Generator: final Surface Materials participation policy. Random preserves the preliminary Surfaces result exactly. Always enables at least two eligible layers at full opacity; candidates are mold, brick, cracks, greenery, wall runoff and the two floor/wall covering layers. Off disables all seven. Wildlife, Surface Drawings and 3D grass are independent and never controlled here. Coverage still decides how much of the level the active layers occupy. An explicit Always is honored at every generator quality tier. Inert until Generate; never part of an AVFX preset snapshot.
cl_avfxgen_profiledefault 0 / 0=Random / 1=Off / 2=Rain / 3=Snow / 4=Ash / 5=Dust / 6=MistAVFX Preset Generator: main atmosphere selector. Random lets the generator pick a weighted identity (including Off, which then always receives a sky or surface theme so the scene is never empty); a fixed choice is honored exactly. Changes nothing until Generate is pressed. Saved to the global Q2PRO-X config; never part of any AVFX preset snapshot.
cl_avfxgen_qualitydefault 2 / 0=Ultra Performance / 1=Performance / 2=Balanced / 3=Quality / 4=Ultra Quality / 5=Extra QualityAVFX Preset Generator: quality envelope of the generated scene. Six tiers from Ultra Performance to Extra Quality; higher tiers unlock more expensive effect families and bigger generation budgets, and reflection families can only be generated at Extra Quality. This is a generator policy selector, not the live cl_avfx_quality: it changes nothing until Generate is pressed. Saved to the global Q2PRO-X config; never part of any AVFX preset snapshot.
cl_avfxgen_skydefault 0 / 0=Random / 1=Map / 2=Weather / 3=Blue / 4=Stars / 5=Space / 6=Nebula / 7=Sunny / 8=MysticAVFX Preset Generator: base-sky family selector. A fixed choice keeps its identity (map sky, weather-driven, blue, star field, space, colored nebula, sunny, mystic) while Full chaos varies its appearance; space/nebula/mystic need Balanced quality, sunny needs Performance — a fixed family below its tier is refused with an explanation. Inert until Generate; never part of any AVFX preset snapshot.
cl_avfxgen_surfacesdefault 0 / 0=Random / 1=Off / 2=Materials / 3=Coverings / 4=Grass / 5=Wildlife / 6=All compatibleAVFX Preset Generator: preliminary surface-family selector. It chooses among material variants, floor/wall coverings, 3D grass and wildlife. The narrower Materials and Wildlife policies make the final decision for those two domains, so their Always or Off state overrides this selector. The generator changes visual state only, never gameplay, damage, contact, blood or audio policy. Inert until Generate; never part of an AVFX preset snapshot.
cl_avfxgen_trafficdefault 0 / 0=Random / 1=Off / 2=All compatible / 3=Impact meteors / 4=Sky meteors / 5=Comets / 6=SpaceshipsAVFX Preset Generator: independent meteors-and-ships selector. Random (default) chooses any tier-allowed subset. Off disables every moving family. All compatible enables impact meteors, sky meteors, comets and spaceships allowed by the quality tier. A fixed kind is exact and disables the other three; impact/sky meteors and comets need Performance, spaceships need Balanced. Inert until Generate; never part of any AVFX preset snapshot.
cl_avfxgen_waterdefault 0 / 0=Random / 1=Off / 2=Water / 3=Puddles / 4=Water and puddlesAVFX Preset Generator: water and puddles selector. Fixed Puddles (alone or with Water) require the Rain atmosphere: a Random main profile resolves to Rain, a fixed incompatible one is refused atomically — the generator never silently changes a fixed choice. Inert until Generate; never part of any AVFX preset snapshot.
cl_avfxgen_wildlifedefault 1 / 0=Random / 1=Always / 2=OffAVFX Preset Generator: final Wildlife participation policy. Random preserves the preliminary Surfaces result exactly. Always enables Wildlife at full opacity and selects Random (all species), so occupied routes can mix every available creature kind. Off disables Wildlife. Materials, Surface Drawings and 3D grass are independent; the coverage-zone selector never changes Wildlife. An explicit Always is honored at every generator quality tier. Inert until Generate; never part of an AVFX preset snapshot.
cl_perf_hud_show_avfx0=hide the section / 1=show the section (default)Show the AVFX section. Only families that are actually switched on appear; a family requested but blocked by a parent or a capability shows one row with its exact reason, and a family that is simply off is omitted rather than drawn as a grey catalogue. When AVFX is globally disabled or the current mod's master is off, the whole section collapses to one truthful status row. The section accent colour is violet.
cl_sp_avfx_lightning_damage0=off (default) / 1=apply lightning damage to nearby monstersMaster toggle for AVFX lightning monster damage. When ON, AVFX storm lightning strikes radial-damage nearby live monsters using rocket/grenade-class damage and a much larger area (~5x grenade launcher). Local single-player and SP DM-training only — no effect in deathmatch, coop, demo playback or remote multiplayer. Player, items, doors, projectiles, triggers and world brushes are NEVER damaged. Bosses included by default. Uses actual AVFX strike positions; visual / audio lightning is unchanged. Game DLL applies damage; stock baseq2/gamex86_64.dll untouched.
cl_sp_avfx_lightning_damage_amountdefault 120 / range 0..1000 / step 1Damage dealt at the strike center. Default 120 matches rocket / grenade base damage. Damage falls off with distance from the strike center using damage * (1.0 - 0.75 * dist / radius) shape — about 25% damage at the radius edge, full damage at the center. Minimum applied damage is 1 when the master is on and amount > 0. Stock light monsters around 20-80 HP die near a direct strike; medium 100-200 HP may die near the center; heavy 300+ HP usually survive one strike; bosses survive many.
cl_sp_avfx_lightning_damage_breakablesdefault 0 / 0=off / 1=damage breakable/explosive objectsAllow AVFX lightning to damage nearby explosive barrels (misc_explobox) and breakable func_explosive brushes using the same amount / radius / LOS / falloff settings as monster lightning damage. Default 0 (off). Independent from cl_sp_avfx_lightning_damage — monsters and breakables can be toggled separately or together. Allowlist is strictly misc_explobox + func_explosive — doors, buttons, triggers and scripted target entities are never affected even though they may have takedamage != DAMAGE_NO.
cl_sp_avfx_lightning_damage_losdefault 1 / 0=no LOS check / 1=require LOSRequire line of sight from the strike point to the monster's bbox center before applying damage. Uses a MASK_SOLID trace, so solid world brushes block damage but other monsters / items / glass do not. Default 1 (LOS required) — lightning does not hurt monsters behind thick walls. Set 0 to allow through-wall radial damage within the radius.
cl_sp_avfx_lightning_damage_radiusdefault 800 / range 0..2048 / step 1 / wuDamage radius in world units. Default 800 is about 5x the grenade launcher splash (160) so a single strike covers a large room. Damage falls off linearly from full at the center to ~25% at the configured radius. Set 0 to disable damage entirely (diagnostic counts as invalid-radius skip). Values above ~1024 are stylized and let one strike clear large areas; clamp is 2048.
cl_sp_avfx_meteor_impact_damagedefault 0 / 0 or 1Master toggle for AVFX impact meteor gameplay damage to monsters. Works ONLY in local single player and SP-training (deathmatch 0, coop 0, single client). Does NOT apply in normal multiplayer / coop / demo. Default OFF (opt-in). Game DLL is authoritative for all gates.
cl_sp_avfx_meteor_impact_damage_amountdefault 260 / range 0..2000 / step 10Peak damage at the impact point. 260 (default) — rocket-class strong hit. Scales linearly with meteor size (radius_scale clamped 0.25..3.0). Falloff cvar drops damage to (1-falloff) at radius edge.
cl_sp_avfx_meteor_impact_damage_breakablesdefault 1 / 0 or 1Allow meteor impact to detonate misc_explobox (exploding barrels) and damage func_explosive (breakable brushes). ON (default). Doors, buttons, triggers and scripted entities are NEVER affected by this gate — only the specific allowlist.
cl_sp_avfx_meteor_impact_damage_falloffdefault 0.75 / range 0.0..1.0 / step 0.05Damage falloff slope. 0.75 (default) — edge of radius receives 25% of peak damage. 0 = no falloff (full damage everywhere in radius). 1.0 = damage zero at edge. Linear: damage = peak × (1 - falloff × dist / radius).
cl_sp_avfx_meteor_impact_damage_knockbackdefault 140 / range 0..500 / step 5Knockback impulse applied to damaged monsters (Q2 T_Damage knockback parameter). 140 (default) — noticeable shove without launching them across the map.
cl_sp_avfx_meteor_impact_damage_losdefault 1 / 0 or 1Require line-of-sight from impact point to target. ON (default) — solid world brushes between impact and monster block damage (MASK_SOLID trace). OFF — radial damage ignores geometry. Trace start lifted +8 wu to clear floor brushes.
cl_sp_avfx_meteor_impact_damage_radiusdefault 640 / range 0..4096 / step 32Damage radius in world units around the impact point. 640 (default). Scales linearly with meteor size (clamped 0.25..3.0). Larger meteors hit a wider area.
cl_sp_avfx_monster_attack_snakesdefault 1 / 0=this direction never happens / 1=enabledLet monsters notice a Snake on their own and attack it with their normal melee, hitscan and projectile weapons. Dormant while the combat master is off. On by default, so enabling the master alone already produces this direction.
cl_sp_avfx_monster_attack_snakes_chancedefault 50 / 0..100 percent (0=never, 100=always)Chance in percent that a given pair starts fighting at all. It is rolled ONCE when a previously inactive pair becomes eligible - never per render frame, per server frame or per bite - so a pair that was rejected does not creep toward certainty over time and the result cannot move with FPS. 0 rejects every pair exactly, 100 accepts every pair exactly. Changing the value applies to the NEXT meeting: a fight already accepted or already rejected is not re-rolled.
cl_sp_avfx_monster_attack_snakes_damagedefault 20 / 1..1000 base damageBase damage of one an accepted monster hit on a Snake, before armour, power armour, godmode, invulnerability and skill scaling. It is direct contact damage with zero knockback: this slider can never become a launch force, radius damage or armour-bypassing damage. Repeated hits of one attack (shotgun pellets, splash, beam ticks) are collapsed to exactly one transaction, so the number here is what one hit costs. SKILL: the number here is the skill-0 value. Survivability and force values are multiplied by 1x / 2x / 3x / 4x at skill 0 / 1 / 2 / 3, the same direction stock Quake II hardens the game with skill (stock scales monster attack chance 0.5x/1x/2x/2x and halves what the player receives on skill 0; monster health is not scaled by skill at all, only which monsters spawn). Because of that stock halving, on skill 0 the PLAYER takes half of the bite damage shown here, exactly as a monster's damage number behaves. Zones, chances, intervals, bite reach and the engagement budget are not force values and stay literal. sv q2px_snake_info prints the multiplier and the resulting values.
cl_sp_avfx_monster_attack_snakes_intervaldefault 1.00 / 0.10..10.00 secondsMinimum time in seconds between two accepted hits of the same fight. Changing it applies at the next authoritative service tick and never retroactively creates damage.
cl_sp_avfx_monster_attack_snakes_zonedefault 384 / 32..2048 world unitsSearch area in world units. A target inside it may be chosen; actually touching it still needs a physical walkable path and the contact reach. Leaving the area does not end a fight instantly: a short hysteresis prevents target flapping.
cl_sp_avfx_monster_retaliate_snakesdefault 1 / 0=no counterattack after a bite / 1=allow counterattackLet a bitten monster strike back at exactly the Snake that bit it, even when monsters do not attack Snakes on their own. It is a separate decision from proactive acquisition and does not roll the proactive chance. It opens only after a bite that produced positive health damage, so godmode, invulnerability or full armour absorption never trigger it, and it reuses the monster damage, interval and search-area controls. It ends on the Snake dying, five seconds without a valid attack opportunity, loss of range or sight, target invalidation, or the combat master going off.
cl_sp_avfx_snake_attack_monstersdefault 1 / 0=this direction never happens / 1=enabledLet Snakes acquire, approach and repeatedly bite monsters. Dormant while the combat master is off. On by default, so enabling the master alone already produces this direction.
cl_sp_avfx_snake_attack_monsters_chancedefault 50 / 0..100 percent (0=never, 100=always)Chance in percent that a given pair starts fighting at all. It is rolled ONCE when a previously inactive pair becomes eligible - never per render frame, per server frame or per bite - so a pair that was rejected does not creep toward certainty over time and the result cannot move with FPS. 0 rejects every pair exactly, 100 accepts every pair exactly. Changing the value applies to the NEXT meeting: a fight already accepted or already rejected is not re-rolled.
cl_sp_avfx_snake_attack_monsters_damagedefault 20 / 1..1000 base damageBase damage of one Snake bites on a monster, before armour, power armour, godmode, invulnerability and skill scaling. It is direct contact damage with zero knockback: this slider can never become a launch force, radius damage or armour-bypassing damage. Repeated hits of one attack (shotgun pellets, splash, beam ticks) are collapsed to exactly one transaction, so the number here is what one hit costs. SKILL: the number here is the skill-0 value. Survivability and force values are multiplied by 1x / 2x / 3x / 4x at skill 0 / 1 / 2 / 3, the same direction stock Quake II hardens the game with skill (stock scales monster attack chance 0.5x/1x/2x/2x and halves what the player receives on skill 0; monster health is not scaled by skill at all, only which monsters spawn). Because of that stock halving, on skill 0 the PLAYER takes half of the bite damage shown here, exactly as a monster's damage number behaves. Zones, chances, intervals, bite reach and the engagement budget are not force values and stay literal. sv q2px_snake_info prints the multiplier and the resulting values.
cl_sp_avfx_snake_attack_monsters_intervaldefault 1.00 / 0.10..10.00 secondsMinimum time in seconds between two accepted hits of the same fight. Changing it applies at the next authoritative service tick and never retroactively creates damage.
cl_sp_avfx_snake_attack_monsters_zonedefault 384 / 32..2048 world unitsSearch area in world units. A target inside it may be chosen; actually touching it still needs a physical walkable path and the contact reach. Leaving the area does not end a fight instantly: a short hysteresis prevents target flapping.
cl_sp_avfx_snake_attack_playerdefault 1 / 0=this direction never happens / 1=enabledLet Snakes acquire, approach and repeatedly bite you. Dormant while the combat master is off. On by default, so enabling the master alone already produces this direction.
cl_sp_avfx_snake_attack_player_chancedefault 50 / 0..100 percent (0=never, 100=always)Chance in percent that a given pair starts fighting at all. It is rolled ONCE when a previously inactive pair becomes eligible - never per render frame, per server frame or per bite - so a pair that was rejected does not creep toward certainty over time and the result cannot move with FPS. 0 rejects every pair exactly, 100 accepts every pair exactly. Changing the value applies to the NEXT meeting: a fight already accepted or already rejected is not re-rolled.
cl_sp_avfx_snake_attack_player_damagedefault 20 / 1..1000 base damageBase damage of one Snake bites on you, before armour, power armour, godmode, invulnerability and skill scaling. It is direct contact damage with zero knockback: this slider can never become a launch force, radius damage or armour-bypassing damage. Repeated hits of one attack (shotgun pellets, splash, beam ticks) are collapsed to exactly one transaction, so the number here is what one hit costs. SKILL: the number here is the skill-0 value. Survivability and force values are multiplied by 1x / 2x / 3x / 4x at skill 0 / 1 / 2 / 3, the same direction stock Quake II hardens the game with skill (stock scales monster attack chance 0.5x/1x/2x/2x and halves what the player receives on skill 0; monster health is not scaled by skill at all, only which monsters spawn). Because of that stock halving, on skill 0 the PLAYER takes half of the bite damage shown here, exactly as a monster's damage number behaves. Zones, chances, intervals, bite reach and the engagement budget are not force values and stay literal. sv q2px_snake_info prints the multiplier and the resulting values.
cl_sp_avfx_snake_attack_player_intervaldefault 1.00 / 0.10..10.00 secondsMinimum time in seconds between two accepted hits of the same fight. Changing it applies at the next authoritative service tick and never retroactively creates damage.
cl_sp_avfx_snake_attack_player_zonedefault 384 / 32..2048 world unitsSearch area in world units. A target inside it may be chosen; actually touching it still needs a physical walkable path and the contact reach. Leaving the area does not end a fight instantly: a short hysteresis prevents target flapping.
cl_sp_avfx_snake_bite_reachdefault 40 / 8..128 world unitsHow close the Snake head must be to the target hull, in world units, before a bite can land. This is contact reach and is deliberately separate from the search area: the search area finds a target, this decides whether teeth can touch it. It scales up safely with the visible Snake size and is still clamped to the range below.
cl_sp_avfx_snake_combat0=off (default) / 1=enable local single-player Snake combatMaster switch of the optional local single-player Snake combat mode. Off is an exact no-op: no candidate scan, no bridge command, no proxy entity, no monster scan and no damage. Requires local single player (deathmatch 0, coop 0, one client, no demo playback) and the Q2PRO-X game DLL from baseq2/q2pro-x; it has no effect in deathmatch, coop, demo playback, on a dedicated server, on a remote server or with a foreign mod DLL. Enabling it produces the complete behaviour at once because every subordinate direction below defaults ON; disable any direction independently. Turning the master off restores every redirected monster target, removes every proxy and leaves no delayed bite.
cl_sp_avfx_snake_combat_debugdefault 0 / 0=silent / 1=rate-limited tracing (session only) (diagnostic, current session only)Session-only diagnostic for the local single-player Snake combat mode. It prints rate-limited session, epoch and outcome tracing on both sides of the local bridge; the read-out itself is the sp_avfx_snake_combat_info command and needs no diagnostic. It is never archived, never written into any config or AVFX preset, and is rejected when it appears in a cfg, so after a restart it is off again unless you enable it in the new session. It costs one integer test on paths that already run.
cl_sp_avfx_snake_combat_tracedefault 0 / 0=silent / 1=full per-tick AI trace (session only, verbose) (diagnostic, current session only)Session-only per-tick flight recorder for the local single-player Snake combat AI. At 1 it prints one [SNCT] line for every live monster and one [SNCR] line for every engaged Snake on every authoritative tick: the current enemy and its kind, the previous enemy, the attack cooldown, the attack state, whether the player is visible to it, which Snake owns it, and its position. It exists because the defects that survive a single assertion are SEQUENCES over time, and tools/analyze_snake_combat_trace.py reads a condump of it and names the monster and the tick at which the AI stopped answering. It is verbose by design, never archived, never written into any config or AVFX preset, and off again after a restart. It costs one integer test when off.
cl_sp_avfx_snake_healthdefault 40 / 1..1000 hit pointsSnake health against monster attacks, in hit points. It belongs to the Snake, not to a particular target or fight: it survives target changes, new fights and save/load while that Snake stays in the fighting set, and it never regenerates. Raising this value does NOT heal a Snake that is already fighting; lowering it clamps the current value down without creating a hit or a death. A Snake that leaves the fighting set entirely and is later admitted again starts at this configured value. SKILL: the number here is the skill-0 value. Survivability and force values are multiplied by 1x / 2x / 3x / 4x at skill 0 / 1 / 2 / 3, the same direction stock Quake II hardens the game with skill (stock scales monster attack chance 0.5x/1x/2x/2x and halves what the player receives on skill 0; monster health is not scaled by skill at all, only which monsters spawn). Because of that stock halving, on skill 0 the PLAYER takes half of the bite damage shown here, exactly as a monster's damage number behaves. Zones, chances, intervals, bite reach and the engagement budget are not force values and stay literal. sv q2px_snake_info prints the multiplier and the resulting values.
cl_sp_avfx_snake_max_engageddefault 16 / 1..32 SnakesHow many Snakes may be in the fighting set at the same time. Snakes already fighting are kept before any newly visible Snake, so looking away from a fight never ends it and a new Snake cannot evict a nearer active one. Lowering the value releases the farthest Snakes first, in a deterministic order, with every monster target restored and no final bite. The hard upper bound is a storage limit, not a recommendation.
cl_sp_avfx_snake_require_losdefault 1 / 0=skip the sight check for acquisition / 1=require sightRequire a clear line of sight before a Snake picks a target, and again immediately before every bite. Independently of this setting a Snake ALWAYS needs a physical walkable path to the target and real contact reach, so switching it off does not let a Snake bite through a wall or reach an airborne, swimming or elevator-borne target.
cl_sp_geo_deform_avfx_sync0=AVFX stays on original anchors / 1=AVFX visuals follow changed surface (default)Makes AVFX visuals such as puddles, snow caps and rain/water rings follow the changed visible surface where possible. Safety checks and accumulation still use the original map geometry.
cl_sp_monster_avfx_contact_amountdefault 1.0 / range 0..5 / step 0.05Overall intensity multiplier for monster contacts. 1.0 (default) baseline; 0 effectively disables emission even when the master is on. Range 0..5. Scales footprint strength, ring radius/strength, splash count, and audio volume together so a single knob produces a consistent louder/quieter mode.
cl_sp_monster_avfx_contact_audiodefault 1 / 0=off / 1=onReuse existing AVFX snow / puddle step sounds for monster contacts. Default 1 (on) for audio/visual cohesion with the monster contact visuals (PO 2026-05-22 deviation from TZ default: «звук шагов должен быть включён по умолчанию когда у нас включены шаги на воде и снегу монстров чтобы было все гармонично»). Set to 0 if monster crowds become too noisy. Respects cl_avfx_audio / cl_avfx_audio_surface_steps / cl_avfx_audio_snow_steps / cl_avfx_audio_puddle_steps masters. Volume lower than the player's footstep gain by design.
cl_sp_monster_avfx_contact_max_distancedefault 1600 / range 256..8192 / step 64 / wuMaximum distance from camera at which monster contacts are emitted (world units). Monsters beyond this distance are tracked (so their step phase / origin history isn't lost) but produce no visible contact this frame. Counted in the skipped-distance diagnostic. Default 1600 wu (~5x grenade splash radius). Range 256..8192.
cl_sp_monster_avfx_contact_max_per_framedefault 16 / range 0..128 / step 1Hard per-frame cap on the number of monster contact emissions. Excess monsters are skipped this frame and counted in the skipped-by-cap diagnostic. Cap is global across snow / puddle / land emissions for the frame. Default 16. Range 0..128. 0 disables emission entirely.
cl_sp_monster_avfx_contactsdefault 0 / 0=off / 1=onMaster toggle: monsters leave snow footprints, puddle ripples / splashes, and landing splashes when stepping through visible AVFX surfaces in local single-player and DM-training. Default 0 (off). No effect in deathmatch / coop / demo playback / remote multiplayer. Player contacts work exactly as before regardless. Sub-toggles (snow_footprints / puddle_splashes / land_splashes / contact_audio) gate individual contact families.
cl_sp_monster_avfx_debugdefault 0 / 0=off / 1=on (diagnostic, current session only)Diagnostic debug spam — when enabled, prints per-frame contact counters via Com_DPrintf on every frame that emits at least one contact. Off by default. Transient (not archived) — toggle via console for live debugging. Use the sp_monster_avfx_contacts_info console command for a one-shot snapshot instead.
cl_sp_monster_avfx_land_splashesdefault 1 / 0=off / 1=onSub-toggle: stronger splash burst when a falling/jumping monster lands into a visible AVFX puddle. Detected via vertical-velocity transition (was negative, now near-zero) plus puddle-coverage check at the landing point. Burst count + amplitude scale with the monster's fall speed magnitude.
cl_sp_monster_avfx_puddle_splashesdefault 1 / 0=off / 1=onSub-toggle: monster step ripples and splash particles in visible AVFX puddles. Speed-scaled (fast monsters produce stronger ripples / visible splashes) and size-scaled (large monsters produce bigger contacts). Uses avfx_spawn_puddle_step_ring_ + avfx_emit_puddle_step_splash_ — same emitters as the player puddle-step path.
cl_sp_monster_avfx_snow_footprintsdefault 1 / 0=off / 1=onSub-toggle: monster footprints on accumulated AVFX snow. Reuses the same persistent footprint overlay buffer (avfx_footprints[]) as the player snow-footprint path. Inactive when cl_avfx_snow_footprints / cl_avfx_snow_accum is off, or when there is no visible snow coverage under the monster.
cl_sp_mutate_liquid_swap_avfx1=contacts follow swap (default) / 0=original contactsSP liquid swap: master for AVFX CONTACT effects following the effective liquid. When ON (default) and cl_avfx 1, weapon impacts, rain ripples, snow contacts and foam on a swapped liquid use the effective material's effects (former water -> lava steam/rings, no water bubbles; former lava -> water splash/rings). When OFF, contacts keep the original liquid's effects. Requires cl_avfx 1 (AVFX master). Local single-player only.
gl_shader_prewarm_avfxdefault 1 / 0=stock keys only (AVFX lazy-compiles), 1=stock + AVFX keys + named AVFX passesREAL include/exclude gate for AVFX-specific shader paths (TZ 2026-06-05 made it a true gate; previously a no-op switch). Effective only when the prewarm policy allows running AND cl_avfx is on. 1 (default) = include AVFX-specific state-bit keys AND the dedicated named AVFX pass programs (stars / meteors / comets / impacts). 0 = prewarm stock/world/postprocess keys only; AVFX programs may lazy-compile on first use — an intentional user-disabled state, reported as such by shader_prewarm_info (include_avfx=0), not a failure.

Game statistics and demos

Variables in this section: 109.

VariableAccepted valuesDescription
cl_demo_analytics_cell_size32 .. 512 world units, default 128Heatmap cell size in world units. Samples are binned into squares of this edge length on the XY plane; a cell's colour intensity follows how many samples landed in it. Smaller = finer detail (more cells drawn). Larger = fewer, bigger blocks. Rebuild triggers automatically when this cvar changes.
cl_demo_analytics_debug0=off (default) / 1=log scans (diagnostic, current session only)Diagnostic logging for the analytics module. 0 = silent. 1 = log scan success/failure with sample/frag/pickup counts and truncation flags when a .mvd2 finishes scanning. Useful for diagnosing missing events or very-dense heatmaps.
cl_demo_analytics_dm2_mode0=off / 1=live POV (default)Strategy for .dm2 single-POV demos (the engine can't replay full arena state — only what the recording POV saw). off — collect nothing, panel stays empty for .dm2 demos. live POV — sample the chase POV position every sample_ms during playback; status label reads dm2 POV only so you know coverage is limited to that player.
cl_demo_analytics_draw_max_cells100 .. 5000 cells, default 1200Hard cap on the number of traffic heatmap cells drawn per frame (both HUD overview and world style). Protects framerate when a dense long-demo scan produces many thousands of cells.
cl_demo_analytics_draw_max_events100 .. 16000 events, default 2000Hard cap on frag-dot + pickup-dot count drawn per frame combined (both HUD overview and world style). Pickups render first, then frags on top — when both exceed the budget the dropped events come from the tail.
cl_demo_analytics_frag_color#rrggbb or named color, default #ff3030Colour of the frag-event dots (HUD panel + world particles). Parsed via SCR_ParseColor.
cl_demo_analytics_mode0=off / 1=traffic / 2=frags / 3=pickups / 4=all (default 0)Master selector for the demo analytics overlay. off draws nothing. traffic renders a heatmap from binned sampled player positions — the full map for .mvd2 (via one-shot pre-scan), POV-only for .dm2. frags draws dots at obituary positions. pickups draws dots at item-pickup positions. all draws all three layers at once. Cycled by the ana: … pill in the demo player overlay.
cl_demo_analytics_mvd_autoscan0=manual only / 1=auto-scan on demo start (default)When on (default), a .mvd2 demo starting playback triggers an automatic pre-scan of the file using MVD_PreScanAnalytics — samples player positions every sample_ms, records all obituary events, records all item-pickup events. Runs in a throwaway scratch parser so live playback is not perturbed. When off, the panel stays empty until you run demo_analytics_rescan manually.
cl_demo_analytics_overview_alpha0.0 .. 1.0, default 0.75Background opacity of the HUD analytics panel. 0 = panel background fully transparent (map/dots still drawn on top of game). 1 = fully opaque black panel. Does not affect world-style particles — see cl_demo_analytics_world_alpha for that.
cl_demo_analytics_pickup_color#rrggbb or named color, default #55ff88Colour of the item-pickup-event dots (HUD panel + world particles). Parsed via SCR_ParseColor.
cl_demo_analytics_sample_ms50 .. 5000 ms, default 250Sampling interval in milliseconds for both the MVD full pre-scan and the .dm2 live POV path. Lower values = denser heatmap but more memory and longer scan time; higher values = coarser heatmap. Sample storage is capped (250k samples) — extremely low values on long demos will truncate and the status label will flag !S.
