Requires ALL of: gl_hdr on, Windows HDR enabled for the monitor under the window, win32egl backend on the ANGLE D3D11 path, and a matching FP16 config preserving depth/stencil/MSAA (stencil is never silently dropped). On any failed gate it falls back to the accepted SDR path and gl_hdr_info prints the exact reason (gl_hdr_off / gl_hdr_output_off / windows_hdr_off / display_not_hdr / backend_not_win32egl / backend_not_angle_d3d11 / backend_no_float_config / backend_no_fp16_surface); true_hdr_output=1 reason=active appears ONLY when the active surface is really FP16. NOTE (HDR-6C): the app's output buffer is linear scRGB UNITS, but Windows desktop composition may apply the system SDR-reference-white presentation scale on top (the Windows HDR 'SDR content brightness' slider); gl_hdr_info reports the active SDR-white value and the effective on-screen paper white. screenshotjxr captures presentation-matched values (what the monitor receives); screenshotjxr_raw captures the exact app output. Changing this requires vid_restart.
gl_hdr_output_debug0=off (default) / 2=above-paper-white heatmap (diagnostic, current session only)True-HDR output developer diagnostic (not archived). 0 = off. 2 = heatmap: pixels brighter than paper white are tinted magenta in the final scRGB encode — verifies every terminal pass goes through the encode and shows where extended highlights actually exceed paper white.
gl_hdr_output_mode0=paper-white parity (default) / 1=extended highlightsTrue-HDR output mapping mode (only acts on a live FP16 surface). 0 = paper-white parity: the picture matches the accepted SDR look anchored at gl_hdr_paper_white_nits (UI white == scene white == paper white; nothing exceeds it). 1 = extended highlights: the final clamp is lifted to peak/paper, so tone-curve values above 1.0 (sun/moon discs, lightning, dialed emissive peaks, exposure) survive as REAL above-paper-white brightness on the HDR display. UI is never boosted in either mode. scRGB mapping per spec: value = nits / 80 in the APP buffer; Windows composition may scale that by the system SDR-reference-white on screen (see gl_hdr_output / gl_hdr_info).
gl_hdr_paper_white_nits100..400 nits (default 200)Brightness assigned to ordinary white world / UI surfaces inside the HDR scene. Raising it lifts mid-tones; lowering it gives more tonal headroom to very bright sources before they clip.
gl_hdr_peak_nits100..2000 nits (default 1000)Target peak display brightness in nits that the tone-mapper aims for. Higher values let bright sources stay brighter before rolling off. On an SDR display this acts as the upper anchor of the tone curve rather than a literal panel brightness.
gl_hdr_saturation0..2 (default 1.0)Optional post-tone-map saturation adjustment. 1.0 is neutral; lower desaturates, higher boosts color.
gl_hdr_scene_format0=auto (default) / 1=RGBA16F / 2=R11F_G11F_B10F (no alpha) / 3=RGBA8 (LDR/debug)Pixel format for the HDR scene buffer. Auto picks the best format that actually passes a framebuffer-completeness probe on this backend. RGBA16F is the safe default and keeps the alpha channel that the sky / god-ray masking relies on. R11F_G11F_B10F is faster and uses less memory but has NO alpha, so it is only valid once the alpha-marker users are moved. RGBA8 forces the legacy LDR buffer (debug). Unsupported choices fall back to RGBA8 with a reason shown in gl_hdr_info.
gl_hdr_tonemap0=linear/clamp (debug) / 1=Reinhard / 2=ACES filmic (default) / 3=Uncharted filmicTone-mapping curve used to compress HDR scene light to the display. Linear/clamp is a debug passthrough. Reinhard is a simple safe roll-off. ACES filmic is the recommended quality curve. Uncharted is an alternative filmic curve.
gl_screenshot_async0=save screenshots synchronously / 1=save PNG screenshots in background thread / 2=save JPG and PNG screenshots in background threadSpecifies if screenshots are saved in background thread to avoid pausing the client. Default value is 1.
gl_screenshot_compression0..9Specifies compression level of PNG screenshots. Values range from 0 (no compression) to 9 (best compression). Default value is 6.
gl_screenshot_formattga/png/jpgSpecifies image format screenshot command uses. Possible values are "png", "jpg" and "tga". Default value is "jpg".
gl_screenshot_quality0..100Specifies image quality of JPG screenshots. Values range from 0 (worst quality) to 100 (best quality). Default value is 90.
gl_screenshot_templatestringSpecifies filename template in "fileXXX" format for screenshot command. Template must contain at least 3 and at most 9 consecutive X in the last component. Template may contain slashes to save under subdirectory. Default value is "quakeXXX".
vid_oled_bar_active_min0..3600 (seconds)Minimum active session time (in seconds) before bar animation is allowed to start. Prevents brief sessions from triggering it unnecessarily.
vid_oled_bar_color_a#RRGGBBPrimary colour for the bar animation (one end of the breathing cycle).
vid_oled_bar_color_b#RRGGBBSecondary colour for the bar animation (other end of the breathing cycle).
vid_oled_bar_delay_sec0..600 (seconds)Delay before the first bar colour transition, in seconds. Lets the bars settle at their initial colour before animation starts.
vid_oled_bar_interval_min0..60 (minutes)Minimum interval between bar colour transitions, in minutes. Slower values are less distracting.
vid_oled_bar_presetsubtle=low contrast / neutral=default / bold=high contrastPredefined bar animation preset. subtle is slow and low-contrast. neutral is moderate (default). bold is more noticeable — use when you want the effect clearly visible.
vid_oled_bar_protection0=static bars / 1=animated barsAnimate the aspect-fit pillarbox / letterbox bars with a slow colour transition so the bars never stay at a static dark grey. Reduces OLED burn-in risk on the bars.
vid_oled_enable0=all OLED features off / 1=suite activeMaster switch for the Q2PRO-X OLED protection suite. When off, the entire suite (bar animation + idle dim + UI breathing) is disabled regardless of the sub-switches below. Intended for OLED displays where static UI can cause burn-in, but safe to leave on for any display.
vid_oled_idle_delay_sec0..3600 (seconds)Idle delay before dimming starts, in seconds. Typical: 60-300.
vid_oled_idle_fade_sec0..60 (seconds)Fade-to-dark duration, in seconds.
vid_oled_idle_hold_sec0..3600 (seconds)How long the screen stays fully dim (HOLD_DARK phase) before optionally transitioning the monitor to DPMS off.
vid_oled_idle_monitor_off0=stay dim but monitor on / 1=DPMS monitor off during HOLD_DARKDuring HOLD_DARK, issue DPMS monitor-off so the panel fully powers down. Opt-in because some desktop setups handle DPMS poorly. Safe on modern Windows monitors.
vid_oled_idle_mute_audio0=keep audio / 1=mute audio while idleMute audio while idle-dim is active (PULSING_DOWN / HOLD_DARK / PULSING_UP). Prevents background music or ambient loops from playing to an empty chair.
vid_oled_idle_protection0=no idle dimming / 1=dim after inactivityDim the screen after a period of inactivity. Three-phase state machine: WAITING (normal) -> PULSING_DOWN (fading) -> HOLD_DARK (steady dim, optionally monitor-off). User activity transitions through RESTORING back to WAITING.
vid_oled_idle_restore_sec0..60 (seconds)Fade-to-restore duration when user activity resumes, in seconds.
vid_oled_ui_cycle_sec0..60 (seconds)UI alpha breathe cycle duration, in seconds.
vid_oled_ui_max_alpha0..1UI alpha breathe upper bound — the brightest point of the breathe cycle.
vid_oled_ui_min_alpha0..1UI alpha breathe lower bound — the dimmest point of the breathe cycle.
vid_oled_ui_protection0=static UI alpha / 1=breathing UI alphaBreathing alpha on protected UI overlays (laghax HUD, server browser, cvar browser). Modulates their background alpha with a slow sine so static UI elements do not sit at the same pixel for extended periods. The breathing factor is exposed via SCR_OledGetUiAlpha() for any overlay that wants to participate.

Highlights and visibility

Variables in this section: 58.

VariableAccepted valuesDescription
cl_pickup_icon_debug0=silent (default) / 1=print classification decisions (diagnostic, current session only)Diagnostic logging for the client-side pickup icon override. When 1, prints which pickup-notify icon / text was observed from the server, which pickup sound was matched (s_health / n_health / l_health / m_health), and which subtype the override resolved to. Off by default; enable temporarily when investigating mis-classification. Does not modify rendering — log lines only.
cl_pickup_icon_override0=use exact server icons / text (no client-side override) / 1=apply override when subtype is identifiable (default)Client-side override of pickup-notify and selected-weapon icons / text for items that the server treats as a single shared entry: distinct subtype icons for Stimpack / Health +10 / Health +25 / Mega Health (when assets are installed in baseq2/pics/), i_armorshard for Armor Shard (instead of the green jacket-armor icon), and w_grenades for hand grenades selected as a weapon (so the selected-weapon HUD slot doesn't look identical to ammo). Pure render decoration: cl.frame.ps.stats[] and cl.configstrings[] are not modified, so demo / MVD recording captures exactly what the server sent and playback applies the override decoration on top. When PNG / PCX / TGA assets aren't installed under baseq2/pics/, the icon override silently falls back to the server-supplied icon, but the text override (Health → Stimpack / Health +10 / +25 / Mega Health) keeps working.
cl_vis_enable0=layer off (no highlights) / 1=layer activeMaster enable for the Q2PRO-X visibility / highlight layer. Controls item, weapon, and player highlighting as a single gate. When off, the layer is completely neutral (no shells, no tints, no scale changes).
cl_vis_items0=no item highlight / 1=highlight itemsHighlight pickup items (weapons, ammo, health, armour, power-ups). Drives the cl_vis_items_style path — shell overlay, colour tint, or both.
cl_vis_items_alpha0..1Item highlight overlay alpha (transparency of the applied tint / shell).
cl_vis_items_brightness0..4 (1 = neutral)Item highlight brightness multiplier; >1 boosts saturation of the tint / shell.
cl_vis_items_scale0.5..3.0 (1 = stock size)Pickup item scale boost applied before submission. 1.0 keeps stock size; larger = more visible from distance.
cl_vis_items_shell_alpha0..1Alpha of the colour-shell pass (RF_SHELL_*) for highlighted items.
cl_vis_items_shell_scale0.5..3.0Scale of the colour-shell pass (ent.scale multiplier applied to the shell entity copy).
cl_vis_items_style0=off / 1=shell overlay / 2=base-model tint / 3=shell + tintItem highlight style. 0 disables. 1 draws a coloured shell only (classic visual look). 2 tints the base model colour. 3 does both.
cl_vis_overlay_batch0/1 (0 = High, 1 = Performance)Graphics quality vs performance for item highlight overlays. 0 = High: stable legacy renderer (default). 1 = Performance: batched glDrawElementsInstanced renderer for higher FPS. Current Performance mode is opt-in and may show frame-to-frame flicker with cl_vis_items_style 3 (shell+tint) until the redesigned combined-safe renderer lands. Local CVAR_Q2PROXCFG_LOCAL — mod-local during normal play, routes to demo_visual cfg during .dm2/.mvd2 playback.
cl_vis_overlay_batch_debugdefault 0 / 0=not requested / 1=batch path was requested at startup outside a config (session only) (diagnostic, current session only)Session-only marker of the experimental item-highlight batch request. When cl_vis_overlay_batch is enabled at startup from the command line, the archived value is reset to the accepted 0 baseline and this diagnostic records the request for the current session. The experimental batched renderer itself is toggled live with cl_vis_overlay_batch; this marker carries no additional behaviour of its own. Never read from a config and never written by any config or preset writer; after a restart it is off again.
cl_vis_player_model_color_<model>#RRGGBB or empty (auto palette fallback)DYNAMIC cvar prefix. For each player model directory (male / female / cyborg / custom players/<model>) you can set an override color used by cl_vis_players_mode = 6 (model). Created lazily — only when you assign a color via the menu, console command, or a pre-loaded cfg. Missing / empty value means: use the automatic palette fallback derived from the model name. Local CVAR_Q2PROXCFG_LOCAL — routes to mod-local cfg during normal play and to demo_visual cfg during .dm2/.mvd2 playback. Commands: cl_vis_player_models_info (list), cl_vis_player_model_color <model> <#RRGGBB/preset/reset> (set/reset one), cl_vis_player_model_colors_reset (clear all overrides).
cl_vis_player_partslegacy; use cl_vis_players_mode 7Legacy compatibility cvar from the first body-part tint prototype. Runtime activation is now controlled by cl_vis_players_mode = 7 (model parts), so cl_vis_players_mode = 6 always remains the old uniform model-colour mode.
cl_vis_player_parts_<male/female/cyborg>_<part>_colorGlobal or named colourPer-model colour choice for male/female/cyborg body parts. <part> is head, arms, torso, legs or weapon. Effective when the colour set is Per model; choosing Global reuses the shared colour for that part.
cl_vis_player_parts_debugdefault 0 / 0=off, >0=overlay (diagnostic, current session only)Developer-only: player-part visibility (highlights) diagnostic overlay. 0=off. Not archived, no menu; zero cost at 0.
cl_vis_player_parts_head_color / arms_color / torso_color / legs_color / weapon_colornamed colourShared colours for the head, arms, torso, legs and carried weapon. The guided menu shows these as named colour choices and applies them live. The weapon colour is used only when cl_vis_player_parts_weapon_source = 1; default carried-weapon tint comes from the existing weapon-highlight palette.
cl_vis_player_parts_head_startdefault 0.86 / range 0.60..0.98Normalized height where the head tint starts. Increase this when the head colour leaks onto shoulders; decrease it if the lower head/neck is not coloured enough. Default 0.86 is tighter than the first Phase-A prototype.
cl_vis_player_parts_softnessdefault 0.035 / range 0.005..0.20Soft transition width for head/torso/legs classifier. Smaller values produce cleaner borders; larger values blend colours more gradually. Default 0.035 reduces head colour bleed on shoulders.
cl_vis_player_parts_source0=global / 3=per modelColour set for player part tinting. Global uses one shared set of head/arms/torso/legs/weapon colours. Per-model lets male/female/cyborg use their own colour choices, with Global as the fallback choice for any part.
cl_vis_player_parts_weapon_source0=weapon palette / 1=customCarried-weapon colour source for model-parts mode. 0 uses the existing weapon-highlight palette (railgun colour from cl_vis_weapon_railgun_color, rocket launcher from cl_vis_weapon_rocket_color, etc.). 1 uses the custom weapon colour from cl_vis_player_parts_weapon_color / per-model weapon colour.
cl_vis_players0=no player highlight / 1=highlight playersHighlight other players with a colour shell / tint, classified per cl_vis_players_mode. Works with all / random-FFA / duel / auto / team / model colouring modes. Off by default. Local CVAR_Q2PROXCFG_LOCAL — mod-local during normal play, routes to demo_visual cfg during .dm2/.mvd2 playback.
cl_vis_players_alpha0..1Player highlight alpha.
cl_vis_players_auto_fallback1=all / 2=random FFA (default)Fallback mode used when cl_vis_players_mode = auto and neither team nor duel can be committed. Stored numerically. Default 2.
cl_vis_players_brightness0..4 (1 neutral)Player highlight brightness multiplier.
cl_vis_players_color#RRGGBBSolid-mode player highlight colour.
cl_vis_players_duel_hold_ms0..10000 (ms)Duel-mode pair-hold time in ms — once the two duelling players are identified, that pair stays locked for this many ms even across brief identification gaps.
cl_vis_players_duel_primary_color#RRGGBBDuel-mode primary colour (first of the two duelling players identified).
cl_vis_players_duel_secondary_color#RRGGBBDuel-mode secondary colour (second of the two duelling players).
cl_vis_players_mode0=off / 1=all / 2=random FFA / 3=duel / 4=auto / 5=team / 6=model / 7=model partsPlayer highlight classification mode. 0=off; 1=all; 2=random FFA; 3=duel; 4=auto; 5=team; 6=model (old uniform colour per resolved player-model directory); 7=model parts (separate head/arms/torso/legs/weapon colours, with detailed controls in Player part colors).
cl_vis_players_scale0.1..5.0 (default 1.0 = stock size)Q2PRO-X player model scale boost. Multiplies ent.scale for every player entity before submission, so players appear larger/smaller than stock. Applied ONLY in single-player (cl.maxclients == 1) or during .dm2/.mvd2 demo playback — on a live deathmatch server (deathmatch >= 1) the value is silently ignored and the stock size is used, preserving competitive parity. In demo playback the recorded match's deathmatch setting does NOT matter: the user is watching, not competing, so the boost applies even for dm recordings. Culling is kept honest by setting ent.cull_scale to the base size so frustum culling still uses the stock bounds. Local CVAR_Q2PROXCFG_LOCAL — during demo playback, edits autosave to baseq2/q2pro-x/demo_visual/q2pro-x.demo.cfg (the same dedicated visual profile as every other local visual cvar).
cl_vis_players_self0=do not tint self / 1=tint selfAlso highlight the local player (visible in third-person / chasecam only).
cl_vis_players_shell_alpha0..1Alpha of the colour-shell pass for player highlights.
cl_vis_players_shell_scale0.5..3.0Scale of the colour-shell pass for player highlights.
cl_vis_players_style0=off / 1=shell overlay / 2=base-model tint / 3=shell + tintPlayer highlight render style — same taxonomy as cl_vis_items_style.
cl_vis_players_team_enemy_color#RRGGBBTeam-mode enemy player colour.
cl_vis_players_team_fallback1=all / 2=random FFA / 3=duel (default)Fallback mode used when cl_vis_players_mode = team and the team adapter cannot commit an assignment (source off, spectators mid-connect, warmup). Stored numerically. Default 3.
cl_vis_players_team_friendly_color#RRGGBBTeam-mode friendly player colour.
cl_vis_players_team_hold_ms0..10000 (ms)Team-mode assignment hold time in ms — keeps the assigned side visible for this long even if the team data source briefly goes stale.
cl_vis_players_team_source0=off / 1=auto (skin-based) / 2=opentdmTeam-mode team detection source. 0 disables the team adapter entirely (team mode then immediately falls back via cl_vis_players_team_fallback). 1 runs the generic auto adapter that infers teams from skin group names (red/blue, team1/team2, tagged skins). 2 targets OpenTDM specifically — reads OpenTDM's team assignment protocol when the server identifies as OpenTDM. Stored numerically.
cl_vis_singleplayer0=multiplayer only / 1=also singleplayerAlso apply the visibility layer in singleplayer. When off, the highlight system only activates in multiplayer maps (cl.maxclients > 1) since most classic SP players dislike shell overlays on AI.
cl_vis_weapons0=no dropped-weapon highlight / 1=highlight dropped weaponsHighlight dropped weapon pickups specifically (subset of items, controlled independently for finer control).
cl_vis_weapons_scale0.5..3.0 (1 = stock size)Dropped weapon scale boost applied before submission.
cl_weaponfx_vis_enable0=WFX layer neutral, legacy cvars only / 1=WFX layer active (default)Master toggle for the Q2PRO-X Weapon Parts Visibility filter. When off the entire WFX layer is neutral (legacy cvars alone decide), so there is zero behavioural drift for users who never touch the new submenu. When on, the source and component toggles below become active.
cl_weaponfx_vis_explosion_light0=hide explosion dynamic light / 1=show explosion dynamic light (default)Dynamic light from explosions (the ex->light field on the explosion_t). When off, the explosion model still draws if cl_weaponfx_vis_explosion_visual is on, but the bright dlight contribution is suppressed.
cl_weaponfx_vis_explosion_particles0=hide explosion particles / 1=show explosion particles (default)Explosion debris / smoke particles (CL_ExplosionParticles). Independent from the main explosion sprite — you can keep the bright flash but drop particles, or vice versa. Legacy cl_disable_particles still applies.
cl_weaponfx_vis_explosion_visual0=hide explosion sprite / 1=show explosion sprite (default)Explosion sprite / model (ex_poly / ex_misc). Gates predicted explosion visuals (CL_GhostRocketExplosion, CL_GhostHBImpact glow) and TE_ROCKET_EXPLOSION / TE_GRENADE_EXPLOSION server visuals. Independent from explosion particles and explosion light below.
cl_weaponfx_vis_hit_markers0=hide HUD hit marker / 1=show HUD hit marker (default)HUD hit marker visibility (the crosshair cross/ring that flashes when you land a hit). When off, the HUD marker no longer appears for TE_DAMAGE_DEALT events. The hit-marker sound level stays controlled by cl_hit_markers (0 none, 1 marker only, 2 marker + sound) so you can keep the sound confirmation while hiding the on-screen element.
cl_weaponfx_vis_hitscan0=hide hitscan beam/tracer / 1=show hitscan beam/tracer (default)Rail beam and any other tracer-like direct-fire visual path. Gates CL_GhostRailTrail for the predicted side and the TE_RAILTRAIL[2] handler for the server side. Sounds (rail fire / impact) stay unaffected.
cl_weaponfx_vis_impact_flesh0=hide blood/flesh impacts / 1=show blood/flesh impacts (default)Blood / flesh-hit visuals. Gates the predicted side (ghost_shotgun_pellet / ghost_cg_bullet flesh particles) and the TE_BLOOD server handler. Kept separate from wall impacts so blood visuals can be hidden independently for screenshot / recording use.
cl_weaponfx_vis_impact_wall0=hide wall impacts / 1=show wall impacts (default)Wall / world impact visuals: bullet sparks, shotgun puffs, blaster wall flash, HB impact glow. Gates both predicted (ghost_bullet_hit_wall, CL_GhostShotgunHit, CL_GhostHBImpact) and server TE handlers (TE_GUNSHOT, TE_SHOTGUN, TE_BLASTER[2]). Ricochet / impact sounds always fire.
cl_weaponfx_vis_muzzle0=hide muzzle flash / 1=show muzzle flash (default)Muzzle flash model / sprite visual. Gates the CL_AddWeaponMuzzleFX / CL_AddPredictedWeaponMuzzleFX / CL_AddMuzzleFX helpers so the muzzle model is drawn only when on. Legacy cl_muzzleflashes still applies on top — setting it to 0 hides muzzles regardless of this cvar.
cl_weaponfx_vis_muzzle_light0=hide muzzle dynamic light / 1=show muzzle dynamic light (default)Dynamic light spawned alongside the muzzle flash (cdlight slot). Independent from the muzzle visual so you can keep the flash model but drop the bright dlight. When off, CL_MuzzleFlash / CL_MuzzleFlash2 zero the dlight slot after the per-weapon switch has set colour and radius.
cl_weaponfx_vis_other0=hide other players' FX / 1=show other players' FX (default)Show weapon FX from other players, monsters, and any foreign source that cannot be confidently classified as our own fire path. Turning this off hides remote projectiles/trails/impacts/explosions while leaving your own unaffected — useful for screenshot captures or low-distraction play.
cl_weaponfx_vis_own_predicted0=hide own predicted FX / 1=show own predicted FX (default)Show local ghost / predicted weapon FX emitted immediately by the Q2PRO-X weapon-predict subsystem (muzzles, projectile ghosts, predicted impacts, predicted explosions). Turning this off hides predicted visuals while keeping the admission gate and suppress-bail untouched — the server copy then passes through per the predict-aware handoff rule (TZ §9.1).
cl_weaponfx_vis_own_server0=hide own server FX / 1=show own server FX (default)Show authoritative server FX that belong to the local player's own fire path (your muzzle flashes, your rocket entity, your rail beam as sent by the server). Turning this off hides your own server copy entirely; combined with own_predicted off, fully silences your own visible fire without breaking sound.
cl_weaponfx_vis_projectiles0=hide projectile models / 1=show projectile models (default)Projectile model and its inherent glow (rocket, blaster bolt, hyperblaster bolt, grenade, BFG ball). Gates both the predicted ghost model (Ghost_AddToScene, ghost_hb_bolts_add_to_scene) and the server entity render path in entities.c. Trails are controlled separately by cl_weaponfx_vis_trails.
cl_weaponfx_vis_trails0=hide projectile trails / 1=show projectile trails (default)Projectile trails for rocket, grenade, blaster, BFG. Gates both predicted (ghost rocket trail in Ghost_AddToScene) and server-side trails (EF_ROCKET/EF_BLASTER/EF_GRENADE/EF_BFG branches in entities.c). Legacy cl_disable_particles bits still apply on top.

cl_demo_item_timers_strip_alphafloat 0..1, default 0.9Item-timer strip background opacity (0 = invisible, 1 = fully opaque). Controls only the strip cells; 3D ghost/label opacity lives in cl_demo_item_timers_world_alpha.
cl_demo_item_timers_strip_pillarbox_workspace0=viewport only (default) / 1=full window incl. pillarboxWhen on (1), the strip's drag-position coordinates are measured from the full window including letterbox / pillarbox bars. When off (0, default), coordinates are relative to the game viewport only. Useful on ultrawide displays with pillarbox rendering to park the strip in the black bars.
cl_demo_item_timers_strip_xinteger, -1 = auto (default)Item-timer strip X position in HUD-pixel coordinates. Normally set automatically by the demo_item_timers_strip_edit drag command; -1 means use the default placement (above the demo player transport bar). Global scope — UI placement survives across demos and is not part of the demo-visual profile.
cl_demo_item_timers_strip_yinteger, -1 = auto (default)Item-timer strip Y position in HUD-pixel coordinates. See cl_demo_item_timers_strip_x for details.
cl_demo_item_timers_world0=off (default) / 1=world only / 2=strip only / 3=bothMaster switch for the demo item respawn timer layer. 0 = off. 1 = world only (translucent ghost models of the real items + projected 3D countdown labels — NO demo player strip). 2 = strip only (demo player items strip with per-item icon + countdown — NO 3D ghosts / labels). 3 = both (world layer + strip layer together). Respawn intervals are derived from observed hidden->visible cycles in the MVD pre-scan — no hardcoded item timers. If no complete cycle has been observed yet, the countdown renders ? instead of a fake value. Ready items never get a 3D overlay — their real model is already drawn by the server. Each item type has its own toggle (cl_demo_item_timers_show_*); armor and powerups default on, weapons default off. MVD2 demos only; .dm2 demos show the honest MVD-only status with no data.
cl_demo_item_timers_world_alphafloat 0..1, default 0.4Opacity of ghost item models and projected countdown labels in the 3D scene (modes 1 and 3). 0 = invisible (also disables the world layer entirely for performance). 1 = fully opaque. Does NOT affect the demo player items strip — the strip has its own independent opacity in cl_demo_item_timers_strip_alpha.
cl_demo_item_timers_world_scalefloat 0.25..3.0, default 1.0Size multiplier for the translucent ghost model in the 3D scene. 0.25 = quarter size, 1.0 = real item size (default), 3.0 = triple size. Text label scale is not affected by this cvar.

Mods, HUD and overlays

Variables in this section: 63.

VariableAccepted valuesDescription
cl_hud_font_mode0=legacy / 1=Iskra Cyrillic (default)Q2PRO-X HUD/local-overlay typography. 0 = legacy conchars. 1 = Iskra Cyrillic fixed-cell (default). Wired trusted surfaces: net autoport indicator, demo item timer screen labels, demo analytics overview panel, screen.c local labels (demo bar progress + time stamp, LAGHAX overlay rows, pred:/phys: extra-line stats), OpenTDM team HUD trusted chrome (title, column headers, '(no teammates)' empty-state, internally-formatted HP/AR/PA/AGE numeric stats). Untrusted/raw paths stay byte-exact: server-supplied layout strings, MVD raw bytes, scoreboard player names, configstring-derived weapon strings, last-message chat, voted strings, server centerprints — these are explicitly NOT routed through Iskra and continue to use the existing legacy / SCR_DrawStringDual UTF-8 safety paths. Atlas-load failure falls back to legacy.
cl_mod_skin_override0=off (default, real server skins) / 1=local override activeQ2PRO-X mod-local player skin override (master enable). When on, the local render path and local sexed-sound resolver can substitute a chosen model/skin for the local player and/or for everyone else, without modifying server userinfo or rewriting CS_PLAYERSKINS. Other clients on the server never see the substitution; scoreboard names and player slots are unchanged; server-side mod gender logic is untouched (mods still derive gender from real userinfo). Local jump / pain / death sexed sounds follow the override when matching assets exist, with legacy fallback. Per-side gates (cl_mod_skin_override_apply_self / _apply_others) refine when each substitution applies. Saved at the active mod level (CVAR_Q2PROXCFG_LOCAL -> <gamedir>/q2pro-x/q2pro-x.cfg), so OpenFFA and OpenTDM keep separate overrides. When the master is on AND the override target model+skin resolves successfully, the chosen clientinfo wins over cl_noskins for that side — the user explicitly opted in.
cl_mod_skin_override_apply_others0=skip others override / 1=apply others override (default)Q2PRO-X mod-local skin override — per-side gate for ALL OTHER players. Default 1. Setting to 0 disables the others substitution while the master cl_mod_skin_override stays on — useful for quickly seeing only the self override.
cl_mod_skin_override_apply_self0=skip self override / 1=apply self override (default)Q2PRO-X mod-local skin override — per-side gate for the LOCAL player. Default 1. Setting to 0 disables the self substitution while the master cl_mod_skin_override stays on — useful for quickly comparing how the others-override looks while keeping the toggle armed.
cl_mod_skin_override_others<empty> (default) / <model>/<skin> (e.g. male/grunt)Q2PRO-X mod-local skin override — value for ALL OTHER players (every entity that is not the local player slot). Format is Quake II's standard <model>/<skin> (e.g. male/grunt). Empty string = no override for other players (real server skins and local sexed sounds kept). Applied when cl_mod_skin_override 1 AND cl_mod_skin_override_apply_others 1 AND the model+skin resolves on disk. This is one global substitution — every non-self player appears and sounds locally as the chosen model+skin/model; per-slot per-player overrides are intentionally out of scope for the first pass. Saved at the active mod level (CVAR_Q2PROXCFG_LOCAL).
cl_mod_skin_override_self<empty> (default) / <model>/<skin> (e.g. female/athena)Q2PRO-X mod-local skin override — value for the LOCAL player. Format is Quake II's standard <model>/<skin> (e.g. female/athena, male/grunt, cyborg/oni911). Empty string = no override for the local player (real server-resolved skin and local sexed sounds kept). Applied when cl_mod_skin_override 1 AND cl_mod_skin_override_apply_self 1 AND the model+skin resolves on disk; otherwise the local player keeps the real clientinfo and the snapshot prints no error. Useful for the TZ scenario cl_mod_skin_override_self female/athena paired with cl_mod_skin_override_others male/grunt on OpenFFA DM. Saved at the active mod level (CVAR_Q2PROXCFG_LOCAL).
cl_modhelp_alpha0..1 (0 = fully transparent, 1 = fully opaque)Opacity of the mod command overlay background. Lower values make the overlay more transparent so you can see the game behind it.
cl_modhelp_compact0=full row spacing / 1=compact spacingUse a compact row layout for the overlay so more entries fit on screen at once (tighter vertical spacing, shorter badges).
cl_modhelp_confirm_dangerous0=dispatch immediately / 1=confirm dangerous commands (default)Ask for confirmation before executing commands flagged as dangerous (kickban, map reload, etc.). The overlay shows an inline yes/no prompt on the row before dispatching.
cl_modhelp_fullscreen0=compact pane / 1=fullscreen overlayExpand the overlay to fill the whole screen instead of a compact pane. Useful for reading long descriptions or showing the pinned list alongside the active page.
cl_modhelp_keep_page0=return to default page / 1=remember last pageRemember the last opened page when the overlay is closed and re-opened within the same session. Off returns to the default landing page each time.
cl_modhelp_pinsstring (comma-separated command names)Comma-separated list of pinned command names the pinned-commands page always shows at the top, regardless of section visibility. Edited via the overlay UI; manual editing is supported.
cl_modhelp_prefer_context_page0=use last-viewed page / 1=auto-pick context page on openWhen opening the overlay, auto-pick the page that matches the player's current context (team / spectator / admin) instead of the last-viewed page.
cl_modhelp_roleauto=detect from server / admin / player / spectator / caster / captainPlayer role filter. auto detects role from server state (scoreboard, userinfo). admin / player / spectator / caster / captain force the overlay into that role view for previewing the commands available to that class.
cl_modhelp_scale0.5..3.0 (1.0 = default)Overlay font and UI scale multiplier. Lower than 1.0 fits more content, higher than 1.0 is easier to read on 4K displays.
cl_modhelp_show_admin0=hide / 1=showShow the admin commands page in the overlay (server management commands).
cl_modhelp_show_aliases0=hide / 1=showShow the command aliases page listing alternative names for commands.
cl_modhelp_show_badges0=no badges / 1=show badgesShow role / danger / category badges next to each command row in the overlay.
cl_modhelp_show_general0=hide / 1=showShow the general commands page (commands available to any connected player).
cl_modhelp_show_pinned0=normal first page / 1=pinned firstShow the pinned commands page first when the overlay opens.
cl_modhelp_show_spectator0=hide / 1=showShow the spectator commands page (observer / chase-cam / scoreboard commands).
cl_modhelp_show_stats0=hide / 1=showShow the stats commands page (personal and match statistics).
cl_modhelp_show_team0=hide / 1=showShow the team / captain commands page (team join, captain actions, weapon drops).
cl_modhelp_show_voting0=hide / 1=showShow the voting commands page (callvote / vote options / remaining time).
cl_modhelp_unavailableshow=always visible / gray=dimmed / hide=omittedHow the overlay displays commands that are currently unavailable in the active role / state. show always displays them normally. gray displays them dimmed. hide omits them entirely.
cl_modhelp_use_local0=server-provided help wins / 1=local override winsPrefer local command database (q2pro.modhelp.local override file) over server-provided help. Useful when you maintain your own curated list or want to override an outdated server-provided entry.
cl_opentdm_team_hud0=hidden / 1=show HUD when on an OpenTDM teamMaster enable for the passive OpenTDM Team HUD. Draws a compact same-team overlay showing each teammate's last-seen health/armor/power cells (from OpenTDM ID view), current weapon (decoded passively from the teammate's player entity, independent of cl_vwep), and optionally the last already-visible say_team line mirrored beside that teammate. Strictly client-only and strictly passive — never auto-issues console commands and never suppresses or alters the original console/chat output. Active only on OpenTDM while the local player is on TEAM_A/TEAM_B (not as spectator).
cl_opentdm_team_hud_alpha0..1 (0.85 default)Team HUD opacity. Independent from scr_alpha. Final alpha is this value multiplied by the OLED UI-protection alpha (so the HUD respects user-level brightness protection identically to the laghax HUD).
cl_opentdm_team_hud_fresh_sec1..120 (default 10, never more than stale threshold)How long passive teammate values remain in the fresh (green) stage before transitioning into yellow and then red. This value is clamped so it never exceeds the stale threshold.
cl_opentdm_team_hud_pillarbox_workspace0=HUD clamped to content rect / 1=allow placement in pillarbox barsAllow the OpenTDM Team HUD to be placed into the pillarbox side bars (aspect-fit free area outside the content rect). Same semantics as the laghax pillarbox toggle.
cl_opentdm_team_hud_scale0.5..2.0 (1 = default)Team HUD text scale multiplier. Independent from scr_scale: higher values make the overlay text larger and easier to read without changing the saved HUD position model.
cl_opentdm_team_hud_show_freshness0=hide freshness / 1=show freshnessShow a freshness / age indicator for passive teammate values. Fresh values are green, then transition to yellow and red as they age; once they pass the stale threshold they disappear from the HUD entirely. Useful because the HUD stays honest about what is still current vs. what has already expired.
cl_opentdm_team_hud_show_powerarmor0=H/A only / 1=H/A/PInclude power-armor cells (P) in the H/A/P column when the last ID-view update reported them. When off, the HUD shows only H/A.
cl_opentdm_team_hud_show_teamchat0=hide team-chat column / 1=show last teammate say_team lineShow the last already-visible say_team message beside the teammate who sent it. Passive HUD mirror only: uses normal PRINT_CHAT delivery, does not inject commands, and does not suppress the original console/chat output.
cl_opentdm_team_hud_show_weapon0=hide weapon column / 1=show weaponShow the current-weapon column for each teammate. The weapon is decoded passively from the teammate's player-entity modelindex2/skinnum. This decoder works independently of cl_vwep — you do NOT need to render teammate vweps to get this column.
cl_opentdm_team_hud_stale_sec4..120 (default 20)Seconds after which passive teammate values expire and are removed from the HUD. Before that they progress through green, yellow, and red freshness stages.
cl_opentdm_team_hud_width12..48 (18 default)Width of the trailing LAST MSG area in character cells. Lets you stretch the overlay horizontally for longer teammate callouts without changing its position.
cl_opentdm_team_hud_xany int (signed), -1 = defaultOpenTDM Team HUD X position in HUD-pixel coordinates. Normally set automatically by the opentdm_team_hud_edit drag command; -1 means use the default placement.
cl_opentdm_team_hud_yany int (signed), -1 = defaultOpenTDM Team HUD Y position in HUD-pixel coordinates. Normally set automatically by the opentdm_team_hud_edit drag command; -1 means use the default placement.
cl_perf_hud0=off (default) / 1=show the HUDMaster switch for the Performance & Budget HUD: a compact column of live occupancy bars and measured CPU/GPU costs for the general frame, dynamic lighting and the AVFX families that are actually enabled. Informative only — it changes no visual quality, no budget and no game or network state. OFF is genuinely off: with 0 the HUD performs no timing call, issues no GPU query, increments no counter, builds no snapshot and draws nothing. It never enables cl_avfx_perf or gl_gpu_timers, and never reads or parses cl_avfx_info.
cl_perf_hud_active_only0=show every selected metric / 1=only active metrics (default)Show only the metrics that are actually doing something right now. A family that is switched off, blocked by a parent, has no valid sample yet, or is simply empty this second is hidden — so puddle, runoff and snow rows disappear when it is neither raining nor snowing, instead of sitting there at zero. This is a PRESENTATION filter, not a collection one: a hidden metric is still measured, so it reappears the moment it becomes active, and a row survives a few seconds of idleness so the column does not blink. Turn it off to see the full selected set including the empty rows.
cl_perf_hud_alpha0..1 (0.85 default)Opacity of the HUD background and text. Independent of scr_alpha: the widget owns its opacity, exactly like the laghax and OpenTDM HUDs. When OLED UI protection is active the final alpha is additionally modulated by it.
cl_perf_hud_ingame_only0=draw everywhere / 1=only on a loaded map (default)Draw the Performance HUD only on a loaded, playing map. With it on the widget stays out of the main menu, the loading screen and the disconnected console, which is where its numbers describe nothing anyway. Visibility and collection are the same decision here: while the HUD is hidden by this option it also stops sampling, so it costs nothing outside a game.
cl_perf_hud_interval0.5..10.0 seconds (1.0 default)How often the HUD publishes a new snapshot, in seconds. Each interval schedules one bounded four-frame sample burst plus a short GPU harvest window; between publications the cached snapshot is drawn as-is, with its age shown in the title. A longer interval is calmer and cheaper; a shorter one reacts faster.
cl_perf_hud_metrics_blackhole0=exclude the group / 1=include the group (default)Include the black-hole group in the AVFX section: the black-hole and consumption masters plus the stage, field and composite GPU intervals. Deselecting the group unsubscribes those query slots entirely.
cl_perf_hud_metrics_fog_clouds0=exclude the group / 1=include the group (default)Include the fog and clouds group in the AVFX section: volumetric fog state, volumetric clouds state and the clouds GPU interval. Volumetric fog has no isolated pass timer and is labelled shared with the world.
cl_perf_hud_metrics_postprocess_misc0=exclude the group / 1=include the group (default)Include the postprocess and miscellaneous group in the AVFX section: the overlay and postprocess GPU intervals, active ambient audio loops and the atlas upload volume in KiB. Deselecting the group unsubscribes those query slots entirely.
cl_perf_hud_metrics_reflections0=exclude the group / 1=include the group (default)Include the reflection group in the AVFX section: mirror surfaces plus the mirror SSR, planar capture and composite GPU intervals, and the reflection capture, puddle and water model-reflection intervals. Deselecting the group unsubscribes those query slots entirely.
cl_perf_hud_metrics_sky_celestial0=exclude the group / 1=include the group (default)Include the sky group in the AVFX section: meteors, meteor trains and particles, meteor impacts and comets against their pool capacities, plus the spaceship, star and god-ray masters. Deselecting the group also stops collecting its probes.
cl_perf_hud_metrics_surface_materials0=exclude the group / 1=include the group (default)Include the surface group in the AVFX section: the Surface Materials master (including wildlife) and the number of packed grass instances submitted this frame. Their shader cost runs inside the world and material passes and is labelled shared.
cl_perf_hud_metrics_water_puddles0=exclude the group / 1=include the group (default)Include the water group in the AVFX section: puddles, puddle rings, runoff streams, foam bubbles, ripples, splashes, surface flow segments and the enhanced-water master, each against its real pool capacity. Deselecting the group also stops collecting its probes.
cl_perf_hud_metrics_weather_particles0=exclude the group / 1=include the group (default)Include the weather group in the AVFX section: rain streaks and close drops, rain impacts, snow flakes and accumulated snow patches, ash and mist, lava steam and the per-frame contact events. Deselecting the group also stops collecting its probes, not just drawing its rows.
cl_perf_hud_pillarbox_workspace0=clamp to content rect / 1=allow the pillarbox barsAllow the HUD to be placed into the pillarbox side bars (the aspect-fit free area outside the content rect). Same semantics as the laghax and OpenTDM pillarbox toggles.
cl_perf_hud_scale0.5..2.0 (1.0 default)Text-size multiplier for this HUD only. Independent of scr_scale: a larger value makes the widget's glyphs bigger without changing the saved position model or any other HUD.
cl_perf_hud_show_budget0=hide the bars / 1=show the bars (default)Draw the segmented occupancy bar column. Each bar has twelve fixed cells: filled cells grow left to right, unused cells stay neutral grey, zero fills none and any positive value fills at least one. Setting rows carry an explicit SET marker so a slider position is never mistaken for a resource budget.
cl_perf_hud_show_cost0=hide the cost column / 1=show it (default)Show the whole cost column - everything to the right of the segmented bars, where each row states what it costs the CPU and the GPU or why that cost cannot honestly be attributed. Off leaves a compact list of names and values, which is what most people want once they have seen the costs a few times. The CPU and GPU switches below are refinements inside this column and do nothing while it is off.
cl_perf_hud_show_cpu0=hide CPU costs / 1=show CPU costs (default)Show the measured CPU cost column. A cost is shown only where a producer owns a real timed interval; everything else prints a dash rather than a fabricated zero. Turning this off also stops the HUD from asking those producers to time themselves at all.
cl_perf_hud_show_general0=hide the section / 1=show the section (default)Show the General / Frame section: frame time and FPS, scene entities and particles against their hard capacities, the AVFX overlay queue, worker threads, and the world/material GPU intervals. The section accent colour is cyan.
cl_perf_hud_show_gpu0=hide GPU costs / 1=show GPU costs (default)Show the GPU cost column. Values come from the existing nonblocking GL_TIME_ELAPSED query ring: availability is checked before every read and the HUD never waits on the GPU. A pass with no isolated interval is labelled shared or not isolated, and a pass with no ready result reads warming or unsupported — never 0.000 ms. Turning this off stops the HUD subscribing to any query slot.
cl_perf_hud_show_in_menu0=hide while a menu is open / 1=stay visible over the menu (default)Keep the Performance HUD visible while a menu is open. The widget draws after the menu, so by default it stays on top of it. Turn this off and the HUD steps aside whenever a menu is open - even on a loaded map - and comes back when the menu closes. While hidden this way it also stops sampling.
cl_perf_hud_show_lighting0=hide the section / 1=show the section (default)Show the Dynamic Lighting section: the effective gl_dynamic mode, dynamic lights against MAX_DLIGHTS, the moving/lightning/map/spawn light slots against their real UBO capacities, flashlight and shadow-caster state, and the radius/softness/alpha/dark-boost settings. Its shader cost is shared with the world and material passes and is labelled as such. The section accent colour is amber.
cl_perf_hud_xany int, -1 = default placementHUD X position in HUD-pixel coordinates. Normally set automatically by dragging in perf_hud_edit; -1 means the default placement.
cl_perf_hud_yany int, -1 = default placementHUD Y position in HUD-pixel coordinates. Normally set automatically by dragging in perf_hud_edit; -1 means the default placement.

Mouse, zoom and controls

Variables in this section: 25.

VariableAccepted valuesDescription
cl_mouse_behavior_mode0=q2pro (current default) / 1=r1q2 (compatibility, backend from m_directinput)Global mouse behaviour mode. 0 (q2pro, default) keeps the current Q2PRO-X path: raw-input backend on Windows, transform = m_filter + (sensitivity + length(delta)*m_accel) + optional m_autosens FOV scaling, lookstrafe && !in_mlooking semantics. 1 (r1q2) is a compatibility mode for players migrating from R1Q2: classic transform (m_filter then sensitivity only, no m_accel, no m_autosens), R1Q2 lookstrafe && in_mlooking semantics. In r1q2 mode the backend is selected by m_directinput: 0 = legacy cursor-centered (GetCursorPos + recenter), 1/2 = DirectInput-like relative (raw-input accumulator, same source as q2pro). Changes are applied live; the backend switches on the next frame and clears any pending delta so the two sources never blend.
cl_zoom_ch_alpha0..1 (default 1.0)Alpha channel (opacity) of the zoom crosshair. Applies whether the color is static or health-driven — the health path fills RGB but leaves alpha to this cvar. Default 1.0 (fully opaque).
cl_zoom_ch_blue0..1 (default 1.0)Blue channel of the static zoom-crosshair color. Ignored when cl_zoom_ch_health is on. Default 1.0.
cl_zoom_ch_green0..1 (default 1.0)Green channel of the static zoom-crosshair color. Ignored when cl_zoom_ch_health is on. Default 1.0.
cl_zoom_ch_health0=static color (default) / 1=color by current healthWhen enabled, colors the zoom crosshair by current player health — same gradient as the base ch_health (red at low HP, green-amber at mid HP, white/blue at full HP). Health lookup happens per-frame in SCR_SetCrosshairColor alongside the base-crosshair update, so the zoom cache is always in step with the live health and no stale frame is ever rendered. When this cvar is off (default), the static color from cl_zoom_ch_red/green/blue is used instead.
cl_zoom_ch_red0..1 (default 1.0)Red channel of the static zoom-crosshair color. Ignored when cl_zoom_ch_health is on. Default 1.0 (full red, matching the base ch_red default) so a freshly-enabled zoom crosshair is immediately visible without tuning.
cl_zoom_ch_scale0.25..8.0 (default 1.0 = native pic size; menu step 0.1)Scale of the zoom crosshair image, in the same units as ch_scale. Computed into a parallel width/height cache via an R_GetPicSize + Q_rint pass when the cvar changes — no per-frame cost at draw time. Only has visible effect when cl_zoom_crosshair_enable = 1 and +zoom is held. Menu range 0.25..8.0, step 0.1.
cl_zoom_crosshair0=none / 1=cross / 2=dot / 3=angleCrosshair style used while zoomed. Identical semantics to the base crosshair cvar (0=none, 1=cross, 2=dot, 3=angle) — loads pics/chN.pcx. Consulted only when cl_zoom_crosshair_enable = 1 and +zoom is held; otherwise the base crosshair is drawn. Value 0 renders nothing for the crosshair during zoom (clean scoping) while still drawing the hit-marker overlay if a hit happens — hit feedback is independent of the reticle.
cl_zoom_crosshair_enable0=off (default; base crosshair stays) / 1=use zoom crosshair while +zoom heldMaster toggle for the Q2PRO-X zoom crosshair override. When off (default), the regular crosshair (crosshair / ch_scale / ch_health / ch_red/green/blue/alpha) stays on during zoom and none of the cl_zoom_ch_* cvars below have any effect — useful for users who want zoom to be a pure FOV + sensitivity change without visual reticle swap. When on, the seven cl_zoom_ch_* cvars below fully override the base crosshair for as long as +zoom is physically held. The swap is edge-driven (tied to the +zoom key state, NOT to the smooth FOV transition) so it flips instantly on key down/up — crosshair style transitions between none/cross/dot/angle don't blend meaningfully, so interpolation would just produce visual garbage.
cl_zoom_fov10..170 (degrees, default 40)Target horizontal FOV used while the +zoom bind is held. The view lerps from the current cl.fov_x down to this value over cl_zoom_time seconds; on release it lerps back. Render-local — does not rewrite the fov cvar and does not persist into saved games. Clamped at runtime so the zoom target never exceeds the current base FOV (zoom-in only; attempting to zoom-out via a larger value is ignored). Works identically in both cl_mouse_behavior_mode = 0 (q2pro) and = 1 (r1q2). The FOV shrink uses a single shared transition clock with the sensitivity scale so the two never desync mid-lerp.
cl_zoom_sensitivity0.1..30 (same units as sensitivity, default 1.0)Target mouse sensitivity when fully zoomed, used only if cl_zoom_sensitivity_mode = 1 (manual). The mouse multiplier lerps from 1.0 at base FOV to (cl_zoom_sensitivity / sensitivity) at the zoomed FOV, so setting this equal to sensitivity leaves the mouse unchanged during zoom, while a smaller value slows the mouse proportionally. Has no effect when cl_zoom_sensitivity_mode = 0 (auto).
cl_zoom_sensitivity_mode0=auto (tangent-ratio, default) / 1=manual (lerp to cl_zoom_sensitivity)Selects how mouse sensitivity is scaled while zoomed. 0 (auto) preserves the on-screen angular feel: per-axis mouse multipliers are computed as tan(eff_fov/2) / tan(base_fov/2) on X and Y independently — a geometrically correct projection ratio that keeps a given mouse movement cover the same visible arc before and after zoom. 1 (manual) linearly interpolates the multiplier from 1.0 at base FOV to (cl_zoom_sensitivity / sensitivity) at the zoomed FOV, giving you a fixed target sensitivity you can dial in by feel. In both modes the scale shares a single transition clock with the FOV lerp so sensitivity and FOV always arrive at their destinations together.
cl_zoom_time0..1.0 (seconds, default 0.0 = instant)Duration in seconds of the smooth zoom-in / zoom-out transition. 0 means instant snap (no lerp). A single transition clock drives both the FOV lerp and the sensitivity-scale lerp so they always move together; if you tap the bind shorter than cl_zoom_time the transition reverses from its current position (no overshoot, no teleport). Capped at a reasonable upper bound at runtime to avoid unusably slow transitions.
cl_zoom_walk0=off (default) / 1=+speed is engaged while +zoom is heldWhen enabled, holding +zoom also virtually holds +speed for as long as the zoom bind is down, releasing it on +zoom release. Reproduces the classic alias +walkon "+speed; +zoom" pattern without forcing the user to wrap the bind in an alias. The injection targets an internal sentinel slot on in_speed rather than stomping the state directly, so it coexists correctly with a real +speed bind held in parallel (e.g. SHIFT): if both the real key and the zoom-injected slot are live, the walk state stays engaged until both are released. Engages on the +zoom press edge — toggling this cvar on while +zoom is already held does not retroactively engage walk; the next +zoom press picks it up. Toggling it off mid-hold still correctly releases the injected +speed on +zoom release (idempotent). Whether walk means slower movement depends on cl_run (the standard Q2 walk/run inversion): with cl_run 1 this gives the expected shift-to-walk feel.
in_enable0/1enable the input subsystem
in_grab0=dont grab mouse / 1=normal grabbing policy / 2=smart grabbing policySpecifies mouse grabbing policy in windowed mode. Normally, mouse is always grabbed in-game and released when console or menu is up. In addition to that, smart policy mode automatically releases the mouse when its input is not needed (playing a demo, or spectating a player). Default value is 1.
m_accel0..5Specifies mouse acceleration factor. Default value is 0 (acceleration disabled).
m_autosens0/1Enables automatic scaling of mouse sensitivity proportional to the current player field of view. Values between 90 and 179 specify the default FOV value to scale sensitivity from. Zero disables automatic scaling. Any other value assumes default FOV of 90 degrees. Default value is 0.
m_directinput0=legacy cursor-centered (donor default) / 1/2=DirectInput-like relativeR1Q2 compatibility cvar. Active only when cl_mouse_behavior_mode = 1 (r1q2). Selects the mouse backend within r1q2 mode: 0 = legacy cursor-centered backend (GetCursorPos relative to window centre + recenter on non-zero delta, same as R1Q2 non-DirectInput path; donor R1Q2 default); 1 or 2 = DirectInput-like relative backend (raw-input accumulator + classic R1Q2 transform, no Windows cursor position involved). Importing an R1Q2 cfg that sets m_directinput will automatically route to the correct backend without any manual sensitivity retune.
m_filter0/1When enabled, mouse movement is averaged between current and previous samples. Default value is 0 (filtering disabled).
m_fixaccel0=off / 1=suppress Windows mouse accel (legacy path only)R1Q2 compatibility cvar. Active only when cl_mouse_behavior_mode = 1 (r1q2) and m_directinput = 0 (legacy cursor-centered path). When non-zero, suppresses Windows mouse acceleration curves while the mouse is grabbed by saving the current SPI_GETMOUSE parameters and writing {0,0,0}, then restoring them on ungrab or mode change. Has no effect on DirectInput-like paths (m_directinput 1/2) because raw-input bypasses Windows pointer precision entirely.
m_forward0..2mouse forward motion factor
m_pitchany floatmouse pitch factor
m_side0..2mouse side motion factor
m_yawany floatmouse yaw factor

Only active on the OpenAL backend while riding the OS default (a specific al_device you pinned is left alone). At most one restart is queued per switch (pending-restart guard); soundinfo prints the follow state, the current default endpoint hash/tail, the last endpoint query status, and the last failure. Default 64 preserves pre-2026-05-22 behavior; raise up to the hard compile-time cap of 512 if sounds drop during heavy rain/storm/AVFX cocktail (PO observation 2026-05-22 — «кажется часть звуков пропадает»). DMA backend (CPU mixer) honors the value exactly; OpenAL backend requests the cvar value from qalGenSources and accepts whatever the driver gave — when the driver caps below the request, soundinfo prints a NOTE «driver limited the count below the requested value». To actually let OpenAL Soft go above its 256-source default, the release alsoft.ini must include sources = 512 (the Q2PRO-X binaural config writer emits this line automatically; release packaging must ship this alsoft.ini). Changes apply only after snd_restart (or any sound system re-init); soundinfo shows cvar value, requested-at-init value, and effective count so the user can see all three. Network God and Ping Adaptation

Variables in this section: 63.

VariableAccepted valuesDescription
cl_network_god_auto_autoport0=deny (default) / 1=allowAutomatic permission: allow scheduling the existing fast RTT port probe for the NEXT connection. It never starts a live-session port scan and never runs during a match.
cl_network_god_auto_confirmed0=not confirmed (default) / 1=permissions confirmedRecords that you have seen and accepted the Automatic permission list. Automatic mode refuses to start until this is set, and only the permission dialog sets it — that is why editing a config alone can never arm automation. Open Network God, Permissions, and use Review and enable Automatic to grant it.
cl_network_god_auto_guardian0=deny (default) / 1=allowAutomatic permission: allow bounded connection recovery after an exact, confident link failure. The Guardian's own limits still apply, and its forbidden reasons — a kick, a ban, a password refusal, your own disconnect, a local stall — are never overridden.
cl_network_god_auto_jitter_shield0=deny (default) / 1=allowAutomatic permission: allow the remote presentation buffer to be sized automatically. It never exceeds cl_network_god_jitter_max_ms and never touches your own player.
cl_network_god_auto_laghax0=deny / 1=allow (default)Automatic permission: allow the accepted adaptive Laghax mode to be enabled for the session while prediction corrections grow. The change is session-only — your own cl_laghax value returns on disconnect or when the mode leaves Automatic — unless you explicitly keep it.
cl_network_god_auto_packetdup0=deny / 1=allow (default)Automatic permission: allow Q2PRO command redundancy (cl_packetdup) to be raised inside the protocol bounds, and only on exact evidence that commands are being lost. Session-only like every other automatic change.
cl_network_god_auto_rebaseline0=keep the old window / 1=restart measurements (default)When a critical LOCAL network setting really changes, or the player runs net_restart, discard the entire older measurement window and learn the connection again. This prevents a socket transition, packet-schedule change, ping adaptation change or prediction-model change from being misdiagnosed as a real network incident. Server commands and ordinary network fluctuations never trigger it.
cl_network_god_cooldown_sec5 .. 300 seconds, default 30Minimum pause between two applied changes, in seconds. It prevents oscillation: after an action is applied and verified, nothing new may be applied until this time has passed.
cl_network_god_debug0=off (default) / 1=log Network God events to console (diagnostic, current session only)Event-based diagnostic logging for Network God: mode changes, connection generations, governor transitions and transport attach/detach. Never prints per packet. 0 = off (default) and costs nothing; the complete current state is always available on demand through network_god_info.
cl_network_god_guardian0=off (default) / 1=onConnection Guardian master. Attempts a bounded reconnection to the SAME server when the connection goes silent while the game itself is still running normally. It never reacts to a kick, a ban, a password refusal, your own disconnect, demo playback, a local freeze, an armed Network Lab or a running port scan, and an explicit refusal stops it for that incident for good. Requires Network God to be on.
cl_network_god_guardian_attempts1 .. 10, default 3Maximum recovery attempts for one incident. After the last one the guardian stops and reports why instead of looping.
cl_network_god_guardian_backoff_ms250 .. 10000 ms, default 1000Pause before the first recovery attempt, in milliseconds. Each further attempt doubles it up to a hard internal cap, so a server that stays down is not hammered.
cl_network_god_guardian_debug0=off (default) / 1=log guardian events to console (diagnostic, current session only)Log Connection Guardian incidents to the console: the measured silence, the threshold that was used, every refusal reason and every attempt. Never prints per packet.
cl_network_god_guardian_silence_ms0 = derive a safe threshold (default), otherwise 1000 .. 30000 msHow long the server must be silent before recovery may start, in milliseconds. 0 derives a safe threshold from the measured server rate and your round-trip time, which is the recommended setting. A non-zero value below 1000 is raised to 1000 so a single lost burst can never trigger a reconnect.
cl_network_god_history_sec30 .. 600 seconds, default 180How much recent history the incident timeline and the reports keep, in seconds. It bounds what is displayed and exported; it does not change how the connection is measured.
cl_network_god_hud0=off (default) / 1=status strip / 2=text / 3=strip + textThe optional in-game Network God status. 0 = off (default): no layout and no drawing at all. 1 = the status strip, a chain of seven circles showing the current stage of the control cycle. 2 = one or two localized text lines. 3 = both. The two presentations are independent; neither requires the other. With Network God itself off, an enabled status draws only a static OFF state and starts nothing.
cl_network_god_hud_alpha0.2 .. 1.0, default 0.90Opacity of the status. The state colours keep their meaning at every value, and every state also carries its own glyph.
cl_network_god_hud_anchor0..8: 0=top left, 1=top center, 2=top right, 3=middle left, 4=middle, 5=middle right, 6=bottom left, 7=bottom center, 8=bottom right (default)Screen corner or edge the status is attached to. The offsets are counted from this anchor, so changing the anchor moves the status without losing your fine positioning.
cl_network_god_hud_auto_hide0=always show / 1=auto-hide when healthy (default)Automatically hide the Network God status after the connection check completes without a problem. A new connection, net_restart, a changed critical client network setting, or a newly detected warning/problem reveals it immediately. Routine periodic background scans do not reopen a settled healthy status. When a real problem clears, a fresh hide delay starts. Opening the Network God overlay or HUD edit mode keeps the status visible for comparison.
cl_network_god_hud_auto_hide_sec1 .. 60 seconds, default 5How many seconds a completed healthy connection result remains visible before automatic hiding. The delay restarts after an explicit connection/rebaseline trigger or after a recovered real problem. Warnings and errors remain visible; routine background collection does not reopen an already hidden healthy status.
cl_network_god_hud_labels0=glyphs only / 1=stage captions (default)Write a short stage name under every circle of the status strip (LINK, OBSRV, DIAG, PLAN, APPLY, VERIFY, GUARD), coloured by that stage's state. The glyphs mean: '-' waiting, '>' working, '+' fine or verified, '!' attention, 'x' trouble or rollback, and a purple 'S' marks synthetic Lab evidence. With captions off only the compact glyph strip remains. The full legend is always available on the overlay's Help tab.
cl_network_god_hud_motion0=static / 1=reduced / 2=smooth (default)How the status animates. Static removes the pulse and the smoothing while keeping every glyph, colour and value. cl_network_god_hud_scale0.5 .. 2.0, default 1.0Size of the status strip, its glyphs and the text line, independent of scr_scale and of every other overlay.

cl_network_god_mode0=off (default) / 1=diagnosis / 2=guided / 3=automaticNetwork God master. 0 = off (default): no measurement, no analysis, no queue, no override and no extra work of any kind — the client behaves exactly as it did without the feature. 1 = Diagnosis: measure and explain only; nothing is ever changed. 2 = Guided: propose one change at a time and wait for your explicit confirmation in the overlay. 3 = Automatic: apply only the changes you permitted under Permissions, verify each one against the measured result and revert it if it did not help.
